dvādaśyāṃ vā caturdaśyāṃ phalāhāro yajet suraṃ(1) /
tyaktvā phalāni dadyāttu kurvan phalacaturdaśīṃ //
192.d:
द्वादश्यां वा चतुर्दश्यां फलाहारो यजेत् सुरं(1) /
त्यक्त्वा फलानि दद्यात्तु कुर्वन् फलचतुर्दशीं //
192.m: or on the twelfth or the fourteenth lunar day, subsisting on fruit, he should worship the god. / Having abstained from fruits, he should give them away, performing the Phala-caturdaśī.

192.s:
caturdaśyāṃ mathāṣṭamyāṃ pakṣayoḥśuklakṛṣṇayoḥ /
anaśnan pūjayecchambhuṃ svargyubhayacaturdaśīṃ //
192.d:
चतुर्दश्यां मथाष्टम्यां पक्षयोःशुक्लकृष्णयोः /
अनश्नन् पूजयेच्छम्भुं स्वर्ग्युभयचतुर्दशीं //
192.m: Moreover, on the fourteenth or on the eighth lunar day in both the bright and dark fortnights, / fasting, he should worship Śambhu, [and] one who observes Ubhaya-caturdaśī goes to heaven.

192.s:
kṛṣṇāṣṭamyāntu naktena tathā kṛṣṇacaturdaśīṃ /
iha bhogānavāpnoti paratra ca śubhāṅgatiṃ //
192.d:
कृष्णाष्टम्यान्तु नक्तेन तथा कृष्णचतुर्दशीं /
इह भोगानवाप्नोति परत्र च शुभाङ्गतिं //
192.m: Taking only a single night-time meal on the eighth of the dark fortnight, and likewise on the fourteenth of the dark fortnight, / he obtains enjoyments in this world, and an auspicious state in the next.

192.s:
kārtike ca caturdaśyāṃ kṛṣṇāyāṃ snānakṛt sukhī /
ārādhite mahendre tu dhvajākārāsu yaṣṭiṣu(2) //
192.d:
कार्तिके च चतुर्दश्यां कृष्णायां स्नानकृत् सुखी /
आराधिते महेन्द्रे तु ध्वजाकारासु यष्टिषु(2) //
192.m: And on the fourteenth [lunar day] of the dark fortnight in Kārttika, one who bathes becomes happy, / and when Mahendra is worshipped upon flag-shaped poles.

192.s:
tataḥ śuklacaturdaśyāmanantaṃ pūjayeddhariṃ /
kṛtvādarbhamayaṃ caiva vāridhānī samanvitaṃ //
192.d:
ततः शुक्लचतुर्दश्यामनन्तं पूजयेद्धरिं /
कृत्वादर्भमयं चैव वारिधानी समन्वितं //
192.m: Then, on the fourteenth [lunar day] of the bright fortnight, one should worship Hari as Ananta, / fashioning [an image] made of darbha grass, accompanied by a water-vessel.

192.s:
śāliprasthasya piṣṭasya pūpanāmnaḥ kṛtasya ca /
ardhaṃ viprāya dātavyamardhamātmani yojayet(3) //
192.d:
शालिप्रस्थस्य पिष्टस्य पूपनाम्नः कृतस्य च /
अर्धं विप्राय दातव्यमर्धमात्मनि योजयेत्(3) //
192.m: Half of the cake made from a prastha of śāli-rice flour / should be given to a Brahmin, and half one should take for oneself.

192.s:
kartavyaṃ saritāṃ cānte kathāṃ kṛtvā(4) hareriti /
anantasaṃsāramahāsamudre magnān samabhyuddhara vāsudeva //
192.d:
कर्तव्यं सरितां चान्ते कथां कृत्वा(4) हरेरिति /
अनन्तसंसारमहासमुद्रे मग्नान् समभ्युद्धर वासुदेव //
192.m: Having listened to the narrative of Hari at the edge of a river, [one should pray] thus: / 'O Vāsudeva, rescue those who are sunk in the great ocean of endless transmigration!

192.s:
anantarūpe viniyojayasva anantarūpāya namo namaste /
anena pūjayitvātha sūtraṃ baddhā tu mantritaṃ //
192.d:
अनन्तरूपे विनियोजयस्व अनन्तरूपाय नमो नमस्ते /
अनेन पूजयित्वाथ सूत्रं बद्धा तु मन्त्रितं //
192.m: Direct [us] into your endless form; adoration, adoration unto you whose form is infinite!' / Having worshipped with this [mantra], and tying a consecrated thread

192.s:
svake kare vā kaṇṭhe vā tvanantavratakṛt sukhī //11//
:e ity āgneye mahāpurāṇe nānācaturdaśīvratāni nāma
dvinavatyadhikaśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
:n
1 yajet svayamiti gha..
2 varṣaṃ bhogadhanāyuṣmānityādiḥ dhvajākārāsu yaṣṭiṣu
ity antaḥ pāṭhaḥ jha.. pustake nāsti
3 bhojanamiti gha.. , ṅa.. , ja.. , jha.. , ña.. , ṭa.. ca
4 kathāṃ śrutveti jha..
:p 224
:ś atha trinavatyadhikaśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
śivarātrivratam
192.d:
स्वके करे वा कण्ठे वा त्वनन्तव्रतकृत् सुखी //11//
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महापुराणे नानाचतुर्दशीव्रतानि नाम
द्विनवत्यधिकशततमो ऽध्यायः ||
:न्
1 यजेत् स्वयमिति घ..
2 वर्षं भोगधनायुष्मानित्यादिः ध्वजाकारासु यष्टिषु
इत्य् अन्तः पाठः झ.. पुस्तके नास्ति
3 भोजनमिति घ.. , ङ.. , ज.. , झ.. , ञ.. , ट.. च
4 कथां श्रुत्वेति झ..
:प् 224
:श् अथ त्रिनवत्यधिकशततमो ऽध्यायः
शिवरात्रिव्रतम्
192.m:
upon one's own hand or upon the neck, one who performs the Anantavrata becomes happy. //11
Thus in the great Purāṇa of Agni, the one hundred and ninety-second chapter, entitled 'The Votive Observances of Various Fourteenth Lunar Days'.
[Footnote]
1. 'one should sacrifice oneself' in manuscript gha.
2. The text beginning with 'a year, possessing enjoyment, wealth, and long life' up to 'upon flag-shaped poles' is not found in manuscript jha.
3. 'eating' in manuscripts gha, ṅa, ja, jha, ña, and ṭa.
4. 'having heard the narrative' in manuscript jha.
Now, the one hundred and ninety-third chapter.
The Votive Observance of Śivarātri.

193.s:
agnir uvāca
śivarātrivrataṃ vakṣye bhuktimuktipradaṃ śṛṇu(1) /
māghaphālgunayormadhye kṛṣṇā yā tu caturdaśī //
193.d:
अग्निर् उवाच
शिवरात्रिव्रतं वक्ष्ये भुक्तिमुक्तिप्रदं शृणु(1) /
माघफाल्गुनयोर्मध्ये कृष्णा या तु चतुर्दशी //
193.m: Agni said: / I shall declare the votive observance of Śivarātri, which grants worldly enjoyment and liberation; hear! / That which is the fourteenth [lunar day] of the dark fortnight between Māgha and Phālguna,

193.s:
kāmayuktā tu sopoṣyā kurvan jāgaraṇaṃ vratī /
śivarātrivrataṃ kurve caturdaśyāmabhojanaṃ //
193.d:
कामयुक्ता तु सोपोष्या कुर्वन् जागरणं व्रती /
शिवरात्रिव्रतं कुर्वे चतुर्दश्यामभोजनं //
193.m: endowed with desire, that is to be fasted on, while the observer of the vow keeps vigil: / 'I shall perform the votive observance of Śivarātri, abstaining from food on the fourteenth [lunar day].

193.s:
rātrijāgaraṇenaiva pūjayāmi śivaṃ vratī /
āvāhayāmyahaṃ śambhuṃ bhuktimuktipradāyakaṃ //
193.d:
रात्रिजागरणेनैव पूजयामि शिवं व्रती /
आवाहयाम्यहं शम्भुं भुक्तिमुक्तिप्रदायकं //
193.m: Through keeping vigil at night alone, as one observing the vow, I worship Śiva. / I invoke Sambhu, the bestower of worldly enjoyment and liberation.

193.s:
narakārṇavakottāranāvaṃ śiva namo 'stu te /
namaḥ śivāya śāntāya prajārājyādidāyine //
193.d:
नरकार्णवकोत्तारनावं शिव नमो ऽस्तु ते /
नमः शिवाय शान्ताय प्रजाराज्यादिदायिने //
193.m: O Śiva, the boat for crossing over the ocean of hell, homage be to you! / Homage to Śiva, the tranquil one, the giver of offspring, sovereignty, and the like;
to the bestower of good fortune, health, learning, wealth, and the path to heaven! / Grant me righteousness, grant me wealth, grant me desires, enjoyments, and so forth!

193.s:
guṇakīrtisukhaṃ dehi svargaṃ mokṣaṃ ca dehi me /
lubdhakaḥ prāptavān puṇyaṃ pāpī sundarasenakaḥ //
:e ity āgneye mahāpurāṇe śivarātrivrataṃ nāma trinavatyadhikaśatatamo
'dhyāyaḥ ||
:n
1 bhuktimuktipradāyakamiti jha.. , ṭa.. ca
2 svargamokṣapradāyine iti ṅa..
:p 225
:ś atha caturnavatyadhikaśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
aśokapūeṇimādivrataṃ
193.d:
गुणकीर्तिसुखं देहि स्वर्गं मोक्षं च देहि मे /
लुब्धकः प्राप्तवान् पुण्यं पापी सुन्दरसेनकः //
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महापुराणे शिवरात्रिव्रतं नाम त्रिनवत्यधिकशततमो
ऽध्यायः ||
:न्
1 भुक्तिमुक्तिप्रदायकमिति झ.. , ट.. च
2 स्वर्गमोक्षप्रदायिने इति ङ..
:प् 225
:श् अथ चतुर्नवत्यधिकशततमो ऽध्यायः
अशोकपूएणिमादिव्रतं
193.m:
Grant me virtues, renown, happiness; grant me heaven and liberation!' / Even the sinful hunter Sundarasenaka attained merit [by this].
Thus in the great Purāṇa of Agni, the one hundred and ninety-third chapter, entitled 'The Votive Observance of Śivarātri'.
[Footnote]
1. 'the bestower of worldly enjoyment and liberation' in manuscripts jha and ṭa.
2. 'to the bestower of heaven and liberation' in manuscript ṅa.
Now, the one hundred and ninety-fourth chapter.
The Votive Observances of Aśokapūrṇimā and Others.

194.s:
agnir uvāca
aśokapūrṇimāṃ vakṣye bhūdharaṃ ca bhuvaṃ yajet /
phālgunyāṃ sitapakṣāyāṃ varṣaṃ syādbhuktimuktibhāk //
194.d:
अग्निर् उवाच
अशोकपूर्णिमां वक्ष्ये भूधरं च भुवं यजेत् /
फाल्गुन्यां सितपक्षायां वर्षं स्याद्भुक्तिमुक्तिभाक् //
194.m: Agni said: / I shall declare [the rite of] Aśokapūrṇimā: one should worship the mountain and the earth / on the full-moon day in the bright fortnight of Phālguna for a year; one comes to share in worldly enjoyment and liberation.

194.s:
kārttikyāntu vṛṣotsargaṃ kṛtvā naktaṃ samācaret /
śaivaṃ padamavāpnoti vṛṣavratamidaṃ paraṃ //
194.d:
कार्त्तिक्यान्तु वृषोत्सर्गं कृत्वा नक्तं समाचरेत् /
शैवं पदमवाप्नोति वृषव्रतमिदं परं //
194.m: On the full-moon day of Kārttika, having performed the setting-free of a bull, one should take food only at night; / one attains the realm of Śiva. This votive observance of the bull is supreme.

194.s:
pitryā yāmāvasī tasyāṃ pitṝṇāṃ dattamakṣyaṃ /
upoṣyābdaṃ pitṝniṣṭvā niṣpāpaḥ svargamāpnuyāt //
194.d:
पित्र्या यामावसी तस्यां पितॄणां दत्तमक्ष्यं /
उपोष्याब्दं पितॄनिष्ट्वा निष्पापः स्वर्गमाप्नुयात् //
194.m: On the new-moon day dedicated to the ancestors, what is given to the ancestors becomes imperishable; / having fasted [on it] for a year and worshipped the ancestors, freed from sin, one attains heaven.

194.s:
pañcadaśyāṃ ca māghasya pūjyājaṃ sarvamāpnuyāt /
vakṣye sāvitryamāvāsyāmbhuktimuktikarīṃ śubhāṃ //
194.d:
पञ्चदश्यां च माघस्य पूज्याजं सर्वमाप्नुयात् /
वक्ष्ये सावित्र्यमावास्याम्भुक्तिमुक्तिकरीं शुभां //
194.m: And on the fifteenth [lunar day] of Māgha, by worshipping the Unborn, one attains everything. / I shall declare the auspicious Sāvitryamāvāsyā, which produces worldly enjoyment and liberation.

194.s:
pañcadaśyāṃ vratī jyaiṣṭhe vaṭamūle mahāsatīṃ /
trirātropoṣitā nārī saptadhānyaiḥ prapūjayet //
194.d:
पञ्चदश्यां व्रती ज्यैष्ठे वटमूले महासतीं /
त्रिरात्रोपोषिता नारी सप्तधान्यैः प्रपूजयेत् //
194.m: On the fifteenth [lunar day] in Jyaiṣṭha, at the root of a banyan tree, having fasted for three nights, / a woman observing the vow should worship the great chaste wife [Sāvitrī] with the seven grains,

194.s:
prarūḍhaiḥ kaṇṭhasūtraiś ca rajanyāṃ kuṅkumādibhiḥ /
vaṭāvalambanaṃ kṛtvā nṛtyagītaiḥ prabhātake //
194.d:
प्ररूढैः कण्ठसूत्रैश् च रजन्यां कुङ्कुमादिभिः /
वटावलम्बनं कृत्वा नृत्यगीतैः प्रभातके //
194.m: with sprouted [seeds], neck-cords, and at night with saffron and other [fragrances]. / Having embraced the banyan tree, with dances and songs at dawn,

194.s:
namaḥ sāvitryai satyavate naivedyaṃ cārpayed dvije /
veśma gatvā dvijān bhojya svayaṃ bhuktvā visarjayet //
194.d:
नमः सावित्र्यै सत्यवते नैवेद्यं चार्पयेद् द्विजे /
वेश्म गत्वा द्विजान् भोज्य स्वयं भुक्त्वा विसर्जयेत् //
194.m: one should offer food to a Brahmin with the mantra: 'Homage to Sāvitrī and Satyavat!' / Going home and feeding Brahmins, having eaten oneself, one should dismiss [the goddess]:

194.s:
sāvitrī prīyatāṃ devī saubhāgyādikamāpnuyāt //
:e ity āgneye mahāpurāṇe tithivratāni nāma caturnavatyadhikataśatatamo
'dhyāyaḥ ||
:p 226
:ś atha pañcanavatyadhikaśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
vāravratāni
194.d:
सावित्री प्रीयतां देवी सौभाग्यादिकमाप्नुयात् //
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महापुराणे तिथिव्रतानि नाम चतुर्नवत्यधिकतशततमो
ऽध्यायः ||
:प् 226
:श् अथ पञ्चनवत्यधिकशततमो ऽध्यायः
वारव्रतानि
194.m:
'May the goddess Sāvitrī be pleased!' [Thus] she attains good fortune and the like.
Thus in the great Purāṇa of Agni, the one hundred and ninety-fourth chapter, entitled 'The Votive Observances of Lunar Days'.
[Page 226]
Now, the one hundred and ninety-fifth chapter.
Votive Observances of the Days of the Week.

195.s:
agnir uvāca
vāravratāni vakṣyāmi bhuktimuktipradāni hi /
karaṃ punarvasuḥ sūrye snāne sarvauṣadhī śubhā //
195.d:
अग्निर् उवाच
वारव्रतानि वक्ष्यामि भुक्तिमुक्तिप्रदानि हि /
करं पुनर्वसुः सूर्ये स्नाने सर्वौषधी शुभा //
195.m: Agni said: / I shall declare the votive observances of the weekdays, which bestow worldly enjoyment and liberation: / When Punarvasu or Hasta falls on a Sunday, bathing with all medicinal herbs is auspicious.

195.s:
śrādhhau cādityavāre tu saptajanmasvarogabhāk /
saṅkrāntau sūryavāro yaḥ so 'rkasya hṛdayaḥ śubhaḥ //
195.d:
श्राध्हौ चादित्यवारे तु सप्तजन्मस्वरोगभाक् /
सङ्क्रान्तौ सूर्यवारो यः सो ऽर्कस्य हृदयः शुभः //
195.m: And in performing a śrāddha on a Sunday, one becomes free of disease for seven lifetimes. / A Sunday on a planetary transit is the heart of the sun, and is auspicious.

195.s:
kṛtvā haste sūryavāraṃ naktenābdaṃ sa sarvabhāk /
citrābhasomavārāṇi sapta kṛtvā sukhī bhavet //
195.d:
कृत्वा हस्ते सूर्यवारं नक्तेनाब्दं स सर्वभाक् /
चित्राभसोमवाराणि सप्त कृत्वा सुखी भवेत् //
195.m: Having observed Sunday [under the asterism] Hasta with food only at night for a year, he enjoys everything; / having observed seven Mondays that coincide with Citrā, one becomes happy.

195.s:
svātyāṃ gṛhītvā cāṅgāraṃ saptanaktyārtivarjitaḥ /
viśākhāyāṃ budhaṃ gṛhya saptanaktī grahārtinut //
195.d:
स्वात्यां गृहीत्वा चाङ्गारं सप्तनक्त्यार्तिवर्जितः /
विशाखायां बुधं गृह्य सप्तनक्ती ग्रहार्तिनुत् //
195.m: Undertaking [the vow of] Tuesday under Svātī, one who eats only at night for seven [such days] is freed from affliction; / undertaking Wednesday under Viśākhā, eating only at night for seven [such days], he dispels afflictions from planets.

195.s:
anurādhe devaguruṃ saptanaktī grahārtinut(1) /
śukraṃ jyeṣṭhāsu saṅgṛhya saptanaktī grahārtinut //
195.d:
अनुराधे देवगुरुं सप्तनक्ती ग्रहार्तिनुत्(1) /
शुक्रं ज्येष्ठासु सङ्गृह्य सप्तनक्ती ग्रहार्तिनुत् //
195.m: Under Anurādhā, [undertaking] Thursday, eating only at night for seven [such days], he dispels afflictions from planets; / undertaking Friday under the Jyeṣṭhās, eating only at night for seven [such days], he dispels afflictions from planets.

195.s:
mūle śanaiś caraṃ gṛhya saptanaktī grahārtinut //
:e ity āgneye mahāpurāṇe vāravratāni nāma pañcavanatyadhikaśatatamo
'dhyāyaḥ ||
:n
1 anurādhetyādiḥ grahārtinudityantaḥ pāṭhaḥ jha.. pustake
nāsti
:p 227
:ś atha ṣaṇṇavatyadhikaśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
nakṣatravratāni
195.d:
मूले शनैश् चरं गृह्य सप्तनक्ती ग्रहार्तिनुत् //
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महापुराणे वारव्रतानि नाम पञ्चवनत्यधिकशततमो
ऽध्यायः ||
:न्
1 अनुराधेत्यादिः ग्रहार्तिनुदित्यन्तः पाठः झ.. पुस्तके
नास्ति
:प् 227
:श् अथ षण्णवत्यधिकशततमो ऽध्यायः
नक्षत्रव्रतानि
195.m:
Undertaking Saturday under Mūla, eating only at night for seven [such days], he dispels afflictions from planets.
Thus in the great Purāṇa of Agni, the one hundred and ninety-fifth chapter, entitled 'Votive Observances of the Days of the Week'.
[Footnote]
1. The passage from 'under Anurādhā' up to 'dispels afflictions from planets' is not found in manuscript jha.
Now, the one hundred and ninety-sixth chapter.
Votive Observances of the Asterisms.

196.s:
agnir uvāca
nakṣatravratakaṃ vakṣye bhe hariḥ pūjito 'rthadaḥ(1) /
nakṣatrapuruṣaṃ cādau caitramāse hariṃ yajet //
196.d:
अग्निर् उवाच
नक्षत्रव्रतकं वक्ष्ये भे हरिः पूजितो ऽर्थदः(1) /
नक्षत्रपुरुषं चादौ चैत्रमासे हरिं यजेत् //
196.m: Agni said: / I shall declare the votive observance of the asterisms; Hari worshipped under an asterism grants desired objects. / First, in the month of Caitra, one should worship Hari as the Nakṣatrapuruṣa.

196.s:
mūle pādau yajejjaṅghe rohiṇīsvarcayeddhariṃ /
jānunī cāśvinīyoge āṣāḍhāsūrusañjñake //
196.d:
मूले पादौ यजेज्जङ्घे रोहिणीस्वर्चयेद्धरिं /
जानुनी चाश्विनीयोगे आषाढासूरुसञ्ज्ञके //
196.m: Under Mūla one should worship the feet; under Rohiṇī one should worship Hari's calves; / and the knees during conjunction with Aśvinī; and under Āṣāḍhā the parts designated as thighs.

196.s:
meḍhraṃ pūrvottarāsveva kaṭiṃ vai kṛttikāsu ca /
pārśve bhādrapadābhyāntu kukṣiṃ vai revatīṣu ca //
196.d:
मेढ्रं पूर्वोत्तरास्वेव कटिं वै कृत्तिकासु च /
पार्श्वे भाद्रपदाभ्यान्तु कुक्षिं वै रेवतीषु च //
196.m: Under Pūrvā- and Uttarā-[phālgunī] the penis, and the waist indeed under Kṛttikā; / the sides under both Bhādrapadās, and the belly indeed under Revatī;

196.s:
stanau caivānurādhāsu dhaniṣṭhāsu ca pṛṣṭhakaṃ /
bhujau pūjyau viśākhāsu punarvasvaṅgulīryajet //
196.d:
स्तनौ चैवानुराधासु धनिष्ठासु च पृष्ठकं /
भुजौ पूज्यौ विशाखासु पुनर्वस्वङ्गुलीर्यजेत् //
196.m: the breasts under Anurādhā, and the back under Dhaniṣṭhā; / the two arms are to be worshipped under Viśākhā, and one should worship the fingers under Punarvasu.

196.s:
aśleṣāsu nakhān pūjya kaṇṭhaṃ jyeṣṭhāsu pūjayet /
śrotre viṣṇoś ca śravaṇe mukhaṃ puṣye hareryajet //
196.d:
अश्लेषासु नखान् पूज्य कण्ठं ज्येष्ठासु पूजयेत् /
श्रोत्रे विष्णोश् च श्रवणे मुखं पुष्ये हरेर्यजेत् //
196.m: Having worshipped the nails under Āśleṣā, one should worship the neck under Jyeṣṭhā; / the two ears of Viṣṇu under Śravaṇa, and one should worship Hari's mouth under Puṣya.

196.s:
yajet svātiṣu dantāgramāsyaṃ vāruṇato 'rcayet /
maghāsu nasāṃ nayane mṛgaśīrṣe lalāṭakaṃ //
196.d:
यजेत् स्वातिषु दन्ताग्रमास्यं वारुणतो ऽर्चयेत् /
मघासु नसां नयने मृगशीर्षे ललाटकं //
196.m: One should worship the tip of the teeth under Svātī; one should worship the face under Śatabhiṣaj; / under Maghā the nose; the forehead in the eyes, under Mṛgaśīrṣa [the forehead];

196.s:
citrāsu cārdrāsu kacānabdānte svarṇakaṃ hariṃ /
guḍapūrṇe ghaṭe 'bhyarcya śayyāgorthādi dakṣiṇā(2) //
196.d:
चित्रासु चार्द्रासु कचानब्दान्ते स्वर्णकं हरिं /
गुडपूर्णे घटे ऽभ्यर्च्य शय्यागोर्थादि दक्षिणा(2) //
196.m: and the hair under Citrā and Ārdrā. At the end of the year, having worshipped a golden Hari / in a jar filled with raw sugar, a bed, a cow, wealth, and the like are the sacrificial fee.

196.s:
nakṣatrapuruṣo viṣṇuḥ pūjanīyaḥ śivātmakaḥ /
:n
1 hariḥ sarvatra pūjita iti ga..
2 śayyāgoścādi dakṣiṇā iti kha.. , ṭa.. ca / śayyāgonnādi
dakṣiṇā iti gha.. , ña.. , ja.. ca / śayyādhenvādi sakṣikā iti ṅa..
:p 228
śāmbhavāyanīyavratakṛnmāsabhe pūjayeddhariṃ //
196.d:
नक्षत्रपुरुषो विष्णुः पूजनीयः शिवात्मकः /
:न्
1 हरिः सर्वत्र पूजित इति ग..
2 शय्यागोश्चादि दक्षिणा इति ख.. , ट.. च / शय्यागोन्नादि
दक्षिणा इति घ.. , ञ.. , ज.. च / शय्याधेन्वादि सक्षिका इति ङ..
:प् 228
शाम्भवायनीयव्रतकृन्मासभे पूजयेद्धरिं //
196.m:
Viṣṇu, identical with Śiva, should be worshipped as the Nakṣatrapuruṣa.
[Footnote]
1. 'Hari is worshipped everywhere' in ga.
2. 'A bed, a cow, clothing, etc., as sacrificial fee' in kha and ṭa; 'a bed, a cow, food, etc., as sacrificial fee' in gha, ña, and ja; 'a bed, a milch cow, etc., with witnesses' in ṅa. / [Page 228]
One performing the Śāmbhavāyanīya votive observance should worship Hari on the day of the asterism corresponding to the month:

196.s:
kārttike kṛttikāyāṃ ca mṛgaśīrṣe mṛgāsyake /
nāmabhiḥ keśavādyaistu acyutāya namo 'pi vā //
196.d:
कार्त्तिके कृत्तिकायां च मृगशीर्षे मृगास्यके /
नामभिः केशवाद्यैस्तु अच्युताय नमो ऽपि वा //
196.m:
in Kārttika under Kṛttikā, and in Mārgaśīrṣa under Mṛgaśīrṣa,
with names beginning with Keśava, or with ‘Obeisance to Acyuta.’

196.s:
kārttike kṛttikābhe 'hni māsanakṣatragaṃ hariṃ /
śāmbhavāyanīyavratakaṃ kariṣye bhuktimuktidaṃ //
196.d:
कार्त्तिके कृत्तिकाभे ऽह्नि मासनक्षत्रगं हरिं /
शाम्भवायनीयव्रतकं करिष्ये भुक्तिमुक्तिदं //
196.m:
‘In Kārttika, on the day of the Kṛttikā asterism, Hari stationed in the asterism of the month
I shall worship; I shall perform the Śāmbhavāyanīya votive observance granting worldly enjoyment and liberation.

196.s:
keśavādi mahāmūrtimacyutaṃ sarvadāyakaṃ(1) /
āvāhayāmyahandevamāyurārogyavṛddhidaṃ //
196.d:
केशवादि महामूर्तिमच्युतं सर्वदायकं(1) /
आवाहयाम्यहन्देवमायुरारोग्यवृद्धिदं //
196.m:
Acyuta, the great form beginning with Keśava, the bestower of all,
the god granting an increase of life and health, I invoke.’

196.s:
kārttikādau sakāsāramannaṃ(2) māsacatuṣṭayaṃ(3) /
phālgunādau ca kuśaramāṣāḍhādau ca pāyasaṃ //
196.d:
कार्त्तिकादौ सकासारमन्नं(2) मासचतुष्टयं(3) /
फाल्गुनादौ च कुशरमाषाढादौ च पायसं //
196.m:
Beginning in Kārttika, [offering] food with kāsāra for four months;
beginning in Phālguna, spiced rice; and beginning in Āṣāḍha, milk rice.

196.s:
devāya brāhmaṇebhyaś ca naktannaivedyamāśayet(4) /
pañcagavyajalesnātastasyaiva prāśanācchuciḥ //
196.d:
देवाय ब्राह्मणेभ्यश् च नक्तन्नैवेद्यमाशयेत्(4) /
पञ्चगव्यजलेस्नातस्तस्यैव प्राशनाच्छुचिः //
196.m:
At night, he should offer the food offering to the god and feed the brāhmaṇas;
having bathed in water with five cow-products, he is purified by partaking of it.

196.s:
arvāgvisarjanād dravyaṃ naivedyaṃ sarvamucyate /
visarjite jagannāthe nirmālyanbhavati kṣaṇāt //
196.d:
अर्वाग्विसर्जनाद् द्रव्यं नैवेद्यं सर्वमुच्यते /
विसर्जिते जगन्नाथे निर्माल्यन्भवति क्षणात् //
196.m:
Every article before dismissal is called a food offering;
once the Lord of the Universe is dismissed, it instantly becomes floral remains.

196.s:
namo namaste 'cyuta me kṣayostu pāpasya vṛddhiṃ samupaitu puṇyaṃ /
aiśvaryavittādi sadākṣayaṃ me(5) kṣayañca mā santatirabhyapaitu //
196.d:
नमो नमस्ते ऽच्युत मे क्षयोस्तु पापस्य वृद्धिं समुपैतु पुण्यं /
ऐश्वर्यवित्तादि सदाक्षयं मे(5) क्षयञ्च मा सन्ततिरभ्यपैतु //
196.m:
‘Obeisance, obeisance to you, O Acyuta! May my sin perish; may merit increase!
May my dominion, wealth, and the like be ever undiminished; and may my lineage not perish!

196.s:
yathācyutastvamparataḥ parastāt sa brahmabhūtaḥ parataḥ parātman /
:n
1 sarvapāpahamiti ṅa..
2 sarvasāramannamiti kha.. , ga.. , gha.. ca
3 māsacatuṣṭakamiti kha..
4 naktaṃ naivedyamarpayediti jha..
5 aiśvaryavittādi mahodayaṃ me iti jha..
:p 229
tathācyutaṃ tvaṃ kuru vāñchitaṃ me mayā kṛtampāpaharāprameya //
196.d:
यथाच्युतस्त्वम्परतः परस्तात् स ब्रह्मभूतः परतः परात्मन् /
:न्
1 सर्वपापहमिति ङ..
2 सर्वसारमन्नमिति ख.. , ग.. , घ.. च
3 मासचतुष्टकमिति ख..
4 नक्तं नैवेद्यमर्पयेदिति झ..
5 ऐश्वर्यवित्तादि महोदयं मे इति झ..
:प् 229
तथाच्युतं त्वं कुरु वाञ्छितं मे मया कृतम्पापहराप्रमेय //
196.m:
Just as you, O Acyuta, are beyond the beyond, the supreme Self become Brahman beyond the beyond,
[Footnote]
1. 'Destroying all sins' in ṅa.
2. 'Food that is the essence of all' in kha, ga, and gha.
3. 'A period of four months' in kha.
4. 'He should offer the food offering at night' in jha.
5. 'Sovereignty, wealth, and other great fortune to me' in jha. / [Page 229]
so make my wish unfailing, O immeasurable one who removes the sin committed by me!

196.s:
acyutānanda govinda prasīda yadabhīpsitaṃ /
akṣayaṃ māmameyātman kuruṣva puruṣottama //
196.d:
अच्युतानन्द गोविन्द प्रसीद यदभीप्सितं /
अक्षयं माममेयात्मन् कुरुष्व पुरुषोत्तम //
196.m:
O Acyuta, O Bliss, O Govinda, be pleased; whatever is desired,
make it inexhaustible for me, O boundless Self, O Puruṣottama!’

196.s:
sapta varṣāṇi sampūjya bhuktimuktimavāpunuyāt /
anantavratamākhyāsye nakṣatravratakerthadaṃ(1) //
196.d:
सप्त वर्षाणि सम्पूज्य भुक्तिमुक्तिमवापुनुयात् /
अनन्तव्रतमाख्यास्ये नक्षत्रव्रतकेर्थदं(1) //
196.m:
Having worshipped for seven years, one obtains worldly enjoyment and liberation.
I shall explain the Ananta votive observance, which grants wealth among asterism observances.

196.s:
mārgaśīrṣe mṛgaśire gomūtrāśo yajeddhariṃ /
anantaṃ sarvakāmānāmananto bhagavān phalaṃ //
196.d:
मार्गशीर्षे मृगशिरे गोमूत्राशो यजेद्धरिं /
अनन्तं सर्वकामानामनन्तो भगवान् फलं //
196.m:
In Mārgaśīrṣa under Mṛgaśiras, consuming cow urine, one should worship Hari
as Ananta; the blessed Lord Ananta gives the fruit of all desires,

196.s:
dadātyanantañca punastadevānyatra janmani /
anantapunyopacayaṅkarotyetanmahāvrataṃ //
196.d:
ददात्यनन्तञ्च पुनस्तदेवान्यत्र जन्मनि /
अनन्तपुन्योपचयङ्करोत्येतन्महाव्रतं //
196.m:
and gives endless [merit] again in another birth.
This great votive observance effects the accumulation of endless merit,

196.s:
yathābhilaṣitaprāptiṃ karotyakṣayameva ca /
pādādi pūjya nakte tu bhuñjīyāttailavarjitaṃ //
196.d:
यथाभिलषितप्राप्तिं करोत्यक्षयमेव च /
पादादि पूज्य नक्ते तु भुञ्जीयात्तैलवर्जितं //
196.m:
and brings about the attainment of all desires and makes it imperishable.
Having worshipped the feet and other limbs, one should eat at night, free from oil.

196.s:
ghṛtenānantamuddiśya homo māsacatuṣṭayaṃ /
caitrādau śālinā homaḥ payasā śrāvaṇādiṣu //
196.d:
घृतेनानन्तमुद्दिश्य होमो मासचतुष्टयं /
चैत्रादौ शालिना होमः पयसा श्रावणादिषु //
196.m:
The fire oblation dedicated to Ananta with ghee lasts four months;
beginning in Caitra, the fire oblation is with rice; in Śrāvaṇa and following, with milk.

196.s:
māndhātābhūd yuvanāśvādanantavratakāt sutaḥ //
:e ity āgneye mahāpurāṇe nakṣatravratakāni nāma
ṣaṇṇavatyadhikaśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
:n
1 nakṣatravratakāmadamiti kha.. , ga.. , cha.. ca / nakṣatravratake 'nnadamiti
gha.. , ṅa.. , ña.. ca
:p 230
:ś atha saptanavatyadhikaśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
divasavratāni
196.d:
मान्धाताभूद् युवनाश्वादनन्तव्रतकात् सुतः //
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महापुराणे नक्षत्रव्रतकानि नाम
षण्णवत्यधिकशततमो ऽध्यायः ||
:न्
1 नक्षत्रव्रतकामदमिति ख.. , ग.. , छ.. च / नक्षत्रव्रतके ऽन्नदमिति
घ.. , ङ.. , ञ.. च
:प् 230
:श् अथ सप्तनवत्यधिकशततमो ऽध्यायः
दिवसव्रतानि
196.m:
Māndhātṛ was born as the son of Yuvanāśva through the Ananta votive observance.
Thus in the great Purāṇa of Agni, the ninety-sixth chapter, named “The Asterism Votive Observances.”
[Footnote]
1. 'Granting desires in the lunar mansion votive observance' in kha, ga, and cha; 'giving food in the lunar mansion votive observance' in gha, ṅa, and ña. / [Page 230]
Now the ninety-seventh chapter.
The Day Votive Observances

197.s:
agnir uvāca
divasavratakaṃ vakṣye hy ādau dhenuvrataṃ vade /
yaścobhayamukhīndadyāt prabhūtakanakānvitāṃ //
197.d:
अग्निर् उवाच
दिवसव्रतकं वक्ष्ये ह्य् आदौ धेनुव्रतं वदे /
यश्चोभयमुखीन्दद्यात् प्रभूतकनकान्वितां //
197.m:
Agni said:
I shall speak of the day votive observances; first I state the cow observance.
He who gives a cow facing both ways adorned with abundant gold,

197.s:
dinaṃ payovratastiṣṭhet sa yāti parasampadaṃ /
tryahaṃ payovrataṃ kṛtvā kāñcanaṃ kalpapādapaṃ //
197.d:
दिनं पयोव्रतस्तिष्ठेत् स याति परसम्पदं /
त्र्यहं पयोव्रतं कृत्वा काञ्चनं कल्पपादपं //
197.m:
and observes the milk observance for a day, attains supreme prosperity.
Having observed the milk observance for three days and given a golden wish-fulfilling tree,

197.s:
datvā brahmapadaṃ yāti kalpavṛkṣapradaṃ smṛtaṃ /
dadyādviṃśat palādūrdhvaṃ(1) mahīṅkṛtvā tu kāñcanīṃ //
197.d:
दत्वा ब्रह्मपदं याति कल्पवृक्षप्रदं स्मृतं /
दद्याद्विंशत् पलादूर्ध्वं(1) महीङ्कृत्वा तु काञ्चनीं //
197.m:
he attains the state of Brahmā; it is known as bestowing the wish-fulfilling tree.
He should give an earth made of gold weighing more than twenty palas,

197.s:
dinaṃ payovratastiṣṭhedrudragaḥ syāddivāvratī /
pakṣe pakṣe trirātrantu bhaktenaikena yaḥ kṣapet(2) //
197.d:
दिनं पयोव्रतस्तिष्ठेद्रुद्रगः स्याद्दिवाव्रती /
पक्षे पक्षे त्रिरात्रन्तु भक्तेनैकेन यः क्षपेत्(2) //
197.m:
and observe the milk observance for a day; the day-observer goes to Rudra.
He who spends three nights in each fortnight eating only a single meal

197.s:
vipulaṃ dhanamāpnoti trirātravratakṛddinaṃ /
māse māse trirātrāśī ekabhaktī gaṇeśatāṃ //
197.d:
विपुलं धनमाप्नोति त्रिरात्रव्रतकृद्दिनं /
मासे मासे त्रिरात्राशी एकभक्ती गणेशतां //
197.m:
attains abundant wealth; the one performing the three-night observance for a day,
eating for three nights month after month, eating a single meal, attains the status of Gaṇeśa.

197.s:
yastrirātravrataṃ(3) kuryāt samuhiśya janārdanaṃ /
kulānāṃ śatamādāya sa yāti bhavanaṃ hareḥ //
197.d:
यस्त्रिरात्रव्रतं(3) कुर्यात् समुहिश्य जनार्दनं /
कुलानां शतमादाय स याति भवनं हरेः //
197.m:
He who performs the three-night votive observance dedicated to Janārdana,
taking along a hundred families, goes to the abode of Hari.

197.s:
navamyāñca site pakṣe naro mārgaśirasyatha(4) /
prārabheta trirātrāṇāṃ vratantu vidhivad vratī //
:n
1 dadyāt triṃśatpalādūrdhvamiti gha.. , ja.. , ña.. ca
2 kṣipediti kha.. , ga.. , gha.. , ṅa.. , ña.. ca
3 yastrirātraśataṃ kuryāditi ga.. , gha.. , ña..
4 mārgaśirasya ceti kha.. , gha.. , ja.. , ña.. ca
:p 231
197.d:
नवम्याञ्च सिते पक्षे नरो मार्गशिरस्यथ(4) /
प्रारभेत त्रिरात्राणां व्रतन्तु विधिवद् व्रती //
:न्
1 दद्यात् त्रिंशत्पलादूर्ध्वमिति घ.. , ज.. , ञ.. च
2 क्षिपेदिति ख.. , ग.. , घ.. , ङ.. , ञ.. च
3 यस्त्रिरात्रशतं कुर्यादिति ग.. , घ.. , ञ..
4 मार्गशिरस्य चेति ख.. , घ.. , ज.. , ञ.. च
:प् 231
197.m:
On the ninth day in the bright fortnight in Mārgaśiras,
a man, undertaking the vow, should duly begin the votive observance of three nights.
[Footnote]
1. 'He should give more than thirty palas' in gha, ja, and ña.
2. 'He should cast' in kha, ga, gha, ṅa, and ña.
3. 'He who should perform one hundred trirātra rites' in ga, gha, and ña.
4. 'And of Mārgaśiras' in kha, gha, ja, and ña. / [Page 231]

197.s:
oṃ namo vāsudevāya sahasraṃ vā śataṃ japet /
aṣṭamyāmekabhaktāśī dinatrayamupāvaset //
197.d:
ओं नमो वासुदेवाय सहस्रं वा शतं जपेत् /
अष्टम्यामेकभक्ताशी दिनत्रयमुपावसेत् //
197.m:
He should recite ‘Oṃ, obeisance to Vāsudeva’ a thousand or a hundred times.
Eating a single meal on the eighth day, he should fast for three days.

197.s:
dvādaśyāṃ pūjayed viṣṇuṃ kārttike kārayed vrataṃ /
viprān sambhojya vastrāṇi śayanānyāsanāni ca //
197.d:
द्वादश्यां पूजयेद् विष्णुं कार्त्तिके कारयेद् व्रतं /
विप्रान् सम्भोज्य वस्त्राणि शयनान्यासनानि च //
197.m:
On the twelfth lunar day he should worship Viṣṇu; in Kārttika he should perform the votive observance.
Having fed the brāhmaṇas, clothes, beds, and seats,

197.s:
chatropavītapātrāṇi dadet samprārthayeddvijān /
vrato 'smin duṣkare cāpi vikalaṃ yadabhūnmama //
197.d:
छत्रोपवीतपात्राणि ददेत् सम्प्रार्थयेद्द्विजान् /
व्रतो ऽस्मिन् दुष्करे चापि विकलं यदभून्मम //
197.m:
parasols, sacred threads, and vessels he should give, and pray to the twice-born:
‘In this votive observance, even though hard to perform, whatever was deficient for me,

197.s:
bhavadbhistadanujñātaṃ paripūrṇaṃ bhavatviti /
bhuktabhogo vrajed viṣṇuṃ trirātravratakatratī(1) //
197.d:
भवद्भिस्तदनुज्ञातं परिपूर्णं भवत्विति /
भुक्तभोगो व्रजेद् विष्णुं त्रिरात्रव्रतकत्रती(1) //
197.m:
let that be made complete by your assent!’
Having experienced worldly pleasures, the performer of the three-night votive observance goes to Viṣṇu.

197.s:
kārttikavratakaṃ vakṣye bhuktimuktipradāyakaṃ /
daśamyāṃ pañcagavyāśo ekādaśyāmupoṣitaḥ //
197.d:
कार्त्तिकव्रतकं वक्ष्ये भुक्तिमुक्तिप्रदायकं /
दशम्यां पञ्चगव्याशो एकादश्यामुपोषितः //
197.m:
I shall state the Kārttika votive observance that bestows worldly enjoyment and liberation.
Consuming the five cow-products on the tenth day, fasting on the eleventh,

197.s:
kārttikasya site 'bhyarcya(2) viṣṇuṃ devavimānagaḥ /
caitre trirātraṃ naktāśī ajāpañcapradaḥ sukhī //
197.d:
कार्त्तिकस्य सिते ऽभ्यर्च्य(2) विष्णुं देवविमानगः /
चैत्रे त्रिरात्रं नक्ताशी अजापञ्चप्रदः सुखी //
197.m:
having worshipped Viṣṇu in the bright fortnight of Kārttika, he rides the celestial chariot of the gods.
Eating at night for three nights in Caitra and giving five goats, he is happy.

197.s:
trirātraṃ payasaḥ pānamupavāsaparastryahaṃ /
ṣaṣṭhyādi kārttike śukre kṛcchro māhendra ucyate //
197.d:
त्रिरात्रं पयसः पानमुपवासपरस्त्र्यहं /
षष्ठ्यादि कार्त्तिके शुक्रे कृच्छ्रो माहेन्द्र उच्यते //
197.m:
Drinking milk for three nights, devoted to fasting for three days
starting from the sixth lunar day in the bright fortnight of Kārttika, this penance is called the Māhendra.

197.s:
pañcarātraṃ payaḥ pītvā dadhyāhāro hy upoṣitaḥ /
ekādaśyāṃ kārttike tu kṛcchro 'yaṃ bhāskarorthadaḥ(3) //
197.d:
पञ्चरात्रं पयः पीत्वा दध्याहारो ह्य् उपोषितः /
एकादश्यां कार्त्तिके तु कृच्छ्रो ऽयं भास्करोर्थदः(3) //
197.m:
Having drunk milk for five nights, eating curd, and fasting
on the eleventh lunar day in Kārttika, this penance called Bhāskara yields wealth.

197.s:
yavāgūṃ yāvakaṃ śākaṃ dadhi kṣīraṃ ghṛtaṃ jalaṃ /
pañcamyādi site pakṣe kṛcchraḥ śāntapanaḥ smṛtaḥ //
:e ity āgneye mahapurāṇe divasavratāni nāma saptanavatyadhikaśatatamo
'dhyāyaḥ ||
:n
1 trirātraśatakavrato iti kha.. , gha.. , ña.. ca / trirātraśatakakṛd vrato iti
ṅa..
2 kārttikasya site prārcya iti kha.. , ga.. , gha.. , ṅa.. , cha.. , ja.. , ña.. ca
3 bhāskaro 'nnada iti kha.. , ga.. , gha.. , ja.. , ña.. ca
:p 232
:ś athāṣṭanavatyadhikaśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
197.d:
यवागूं यावकं शाकं दधि क्षीरं घृतं जलं /
पञ्चम्यादि सिते पक्षे कृच्छ्रः शान्तपनः स्मृतः //
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महपुराणे दिवसव्रतानि नाम सप्तनवत्यधिकशततमो
ऽध्यायः ||
:न्
1 त्रिरात्रशतकव्रतो इति ख.. , घ.. , ञ.. च / त्रिरात्रशतककृद् व्रतो इति
ङ..
2 कार्त्तिकस्य सिते प्रार्च्य इति ख.. , ग.. , घ.. , ङ.. , छ.. , ज.. , ञ.. च
3 भास्करो ऽन्नद इति ख.. , ग.. , घ.. , ज.. , ञ.. च
:प् 232
:श् अथाष्टनवत्यधिकशततमो ऽध्यायः
197.m:
Barley gruel, barley food, vegetables, curd, milk, ghee, and water [in succession]
starting on the fifth lunar day in the bright fortnight: this is known as the Śāntapana penance.
Thus in the great Purāṇa of Agni, the ninety-seventh chapter, named “The Day Votive Observances.”
[Footnote]
1. 'The votary of a hundred trirātra rites' in kha, gha, and ña; 'one performing a hundred trirātra rites, a votary' in ṅa.
2. 'Having worshipped during the bright fortnight of Kārttika' in kha, ga, gha, ṅa, cha, ja, and ña.
3. 'The Sun, giver of food' in kha, ga, gha, ja, and ña. / [Page 232]
Now begins the one hundred and ninety-eighth chapter.

198.s:
māsavratāni
agnir uvāca
māsavratakamākhyāsye bhuktimuktipradāyakaṃ /
āṣāḍhādicaturmāsamabhyaṅgaṃ varjayet sudhīḥ //
198.d:
मासव्रतानि
अग्निर् उवाच
मासव्रतकमाख्यास्ये भुक्तिमुक्तिप्रदायकं /
आषाढादिचतुर्मासमभ्यङ्गं वर्जयेत् सुधीः //
198.m:
The monthly votive observances.
Agni said:
I shall explain the monthly votive observance that bestows worldly enjoyment and liberation.
For four months, beginning with Āṣāḍha, the wise person should avoid oil baths.

198.s:
vaiśākhe puṣpalavaṇantyaktvā godo nṛpo bhavet /
godo māsopavāsī ca(1) bhīmavratakaro hariḥ(2) //
198.d:
वैशाखे पुष्पलवणन्त्यक्त्वा गोदो नृपो भवेत् /
गोदो मासोपवासी च(1) भीमव्रतकरो हरिः(2) //
198.m:
By giving up flowers and salt in Vaiśākha, one who gives a cow becomes a king.
One who gives a cow and fasts for a month, observing the Bhīma votive observance, becomes Hari.

198.s:
āṣāḍhādicaturmāsaṃ prātaḥsnāyī ca viṣṇugaḥ /
māghe māsyatha caitre vā guḍadhenuprado bhavet //
198.d:
आषाढादिचतुर्मासं प्रातःस्नायी च विष्णुगः /
माघे मास्यथ चैत्रे वा गुडधेनुप्रदो भवेत् //
198.m:
Bathing in the morning for the four months beginning with Āṣāḍha, one goes to Viṣṇu.
In the month of Māgha or in Caitra, one should make a gift of an effigy cow made of jaggery.

Observing the jaggery vow on the third lunar day, the great observer of vows becomes the lord of Gaurī.
Eating only at night during the months beginning with Mārgaśīrṣa, one partakes of Viṣṇu’s realm.

198.s:
ekabhaktavratī tadvad dvādaśīvratakaṃ pṛṭhak(3) /
phalavratī caturmāsaṃ phalaṃ tyaktvā pradāpayet //
198.d:
एकभक्तव्रती तद्वद् द्वादशीव्रतकं पृठक्(3) /
फलव्रती चतुर्मासं फलं त्यक्त्वा प्रदापयेत् //
198.m:
Likewise, one who observes the single-meal vow [attains the same]; the votive observance of the twelfth lunar day is distinct.
Observing the fruit vow for four months, one should give up fruit and give it away.

198.s:
śrāvaṇādicaturmāsaṃ vrataiḥ sarvaṃ labhedvratī /
āṣāḍhasya site pakṣe ekādaśyāmupoṣitaḥ //
198.d:
श्रावणादिचतुर्मासं व्रतैः सर्वं लभेद्व्रती /
आषाढस्य सिते पक्षे एकादश्यामुपोषितः //
198.m:
During the four months beginning with Śrāvaṇa, the observer of vows obtains everything through votive observances.
Fasting on the eleventh lunar day in the bright fortnight of Āṣāḍha,

198.s:
cāturmāsyavratānāntu kurvīta parikalpanaṃ /
āṣāḍhyāñcātha saṅkrāntau karkaṭasya(4) hariṃ yajet //
198.d:
चातुर्मास्यव्रतानान्तु कुर्वीत परिकल्पनं /
आषाढ्याञ्चाथ सङ्क्रान्तौ कर्कटस्य(4) हरिं यजेत् //
198.m:
one should make the resolution for the four-month votive observances.
On the full moon of Āṣāḍha, or at the solstice of Cancer, one should worship Hari:

198.s:
idaṃ vrataṃ mayā deva gṛhītaṃ puratastava /
:n
1 māse yavāśo ceti kha..
2 bhīmavrataparo haririti ṅa..
3 dvādaśīvratakaṃ paramiti ṅa..
4 āṣāḍhagaṃ vṛṣasaṅkrāntyāṃ karkaṭe ceti jha..
:p 233
nirvighnāṃ siddhimāyātu prasanne tvayi keśava //
198.d:
इदं व्रतं मया देव गृहीतं पुरतस्तव /
:न्
1 मासे यवाशो चेति ख..
2 भीमव्रतपरो हरिरिति ङ..
3 द्वादशीव्रतकं परमिति ङ..
4 आषाढगं वृषसङ्क्रान्त्यां कर्कटे चेति झ..
:प् 233
निर्विघ्नां सिद्धिमायातु प्रसन्ने त्वयि केशव //
198.m:
‘O God, this votive observance has been undertaken by me before you;
[Footnote]
[Variant reading:] "māse yavāśo ca" in manuscript kha.
[Variant reading:] "bhīmavrataparo hariḥ" in manuscript ṅa.
[Variant reading:] "dvādaśīvratakaṃ param" in manuscript ṅa.
[Variant reading:] "āṣāḍhagaṃ vṛṣasaṅkrāntyāṃ karkaṭe ca" in manuscript jha.
may it reach an obstacle-free completion, Keśava, when you are pleased.

198.s:
gṛhīte 'smin vrate deva yadyapūrṇe mriye hy ahaṃ /
tanme bhavatu sampūrṇaṃ tvatprasādājjanārdana //
198.d:
गृहीते ऽस्मिन् व्रते देव यद्यपूर्णे म्रिये ह्य् अहं /
तन्मे भवतु सम्पूर्णं त्वत्प्रसादाज्जनार्दन //
198.m:
O God, if I should die while this votive observance is undertaken but incomplete,
let it become complete for me, Janārdana, by your grace.’

198.s:
māṃsādi tyaktvā(1) vipraḥ syāttailatyāgī hariṃ yajet /
ekāntaropavāsī ca trirātraṃ viṣṇulokabhāk //
198.d:
मांसादि त्यक्त्वा(1) विप्रः स्यात्तैलत्यागी हरिं यजेत् /
एकान्तरोपवासी च त्रिरात्रं विष्णुलोकभाक् //
198.m:
Giving up meat and the like, a twice-born becomes [purified]; renouncing oil, he should worship Hari.
Fasting on alternate days or for three nights, he partakes of Viṣṇu’s realm.

198.s:
cāndrāyaṇī viṣṇulokī maunī syān muktibhājanaṃ /
prājāpatyavratī svargī śaktuyāvakabhakṣakaḥ //
198.d:
चान्द्रायणी विष्णुलोकी मौनी स्यान् मुक्तिभाजनं /
प्राजापत्यव्रती स्वर्गी शक्तुयावकभक्षकः //
198.m:
One performing the cāndrāyaṇa penance reaches Viṣṇu’s realm; observing silence, one becomes a vessel of liberation.
One performing the prājāpatya vow attains heaven, eating barley meal and barley gruel.

198.s:
gugdhādyāhāravān svargī pañcagavyāmbubhktathā /
śākamūlaphalāhārī naro viṣṇupurīṃ vrajet(2) //
198.d:
गुग्धाद्याहारवान् स्वर्गी पञ्चगव्याम्बुभ्क्तथा /
शाकमूलफलाहारी नरो विष्णुपुरीं व्रजेत्(2) //
198.m:
One whose food is milk and similar products attains heaven, as does one who consumes the five products of the cow and water.
A person eating vegetables, roots, and fruits goes to the city of Viṣṇu.

198.s:
māṃsavarjī yavāhāro rasavarjī hariṃ vrajet /
kaumudavratamākhyāsye āśvine samupoṣitaḥ //
198.d:
मांसवर्जी यवाहारो रसवर्जी हरिं व्रजेत् /
कौमुदव्रतमाख्यास्ये आश्विने समुपोषितः //
198.m:
Abstaining from meat, eating barley, and giving up savory liquids, one goes to Hari.
I shall explain the Kaumuda votive observance: fasting in Āśvina,

198.s:
dvādaśyāṃ pūjayedviṣṇuṃ pralipyābjotpalādibhiḥ /
ghṛtena tilatailena dīpanaivedyamarpayet //
198.d:
द्वादश्यां पूजयेद्विष्णुं प्रलिप्याब्जोत्पलादिभिः /
घृतेन तिलतैलेन दीपनैवेद्यमर्पयेत् //
198.m:
one should worship Viṣṇu on the twelfth lunar day, anointing [the icon] with blue and white lotuses and the like,
and should offer lamps and food-offerings prepared with ghee and sesame oil.

198.s:
oṃ namo vāsudevāya mālatyā mālayā yajet /
dharmakāmārthamokṣāṃś ca prāpnuyāt kaumudavratī //
198.d:
ओं नमो वासुदेवाय मालत्या मालया यजेत् /
धर्मकामार्थमोक्षांश् च प्राप्नुयात् कौमुदव्रती //
198.m:
One should worship with [the mantra] ‘Om, homage to Vāsudeva’ and with a garland of jasmine flowers;
the observer of the Kaumuda vow will obtain virtue, pleasure, wealth, and liberation.

198.s:
sarvaṃ labheddhariṃ prārcya māsopavāsakavratī /
:e ity āgneye mahāpurāṇe māsavratāni nāma
aṣṭanavatyadhikaśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
:n
1 matsyādi tyaktveti kha.. , gha.. , cha.. ca / matsyatyāgī tu iti ṅa.
2 viṣṇupuraṃ vrajediti kha.. , ṭa.. ca
:p 234
:ś athaikonaśatādhikaśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
nānāvratāni
198.d:
सर्वं लभेद्धरिं प्रार्च्य मासोपवासकव्रती /
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महापुराणे मासव्रतानि नाम
अष्टनवत्यधिकशततमो ऽध्यायः ||
:न्
1 मत्स्यादि त्यक्त्वेति ख.. , घ.. , छ.. च / मत्स्यत्यागी तु इति ङ.
2 विष्णुपुरं व्रजेदिति ख.. , ट.. च
:प् 234
:श् अथैकोनशताधिकशततमो ऽध्यायः
नानाव्रतानि
198.m:
Worshipping Hari, one who observes the monthly fast obtains everything.
Thus in the Great Purāṇa of Agni, the one hundred and ninety-eighth chapter, entitled ‘The Monthly Votive Observances.’
[Variant reading:] "matsyādi tyaktvā" in manuscripts kha, gha, and cha; "matsyatyāgī tu" in manuscript ṅa.
[Variant reading:] "viṣṇupuraṃ vrajet" in manuscripts kha and ṭa.
Now begins the one hundred and ninety-ninth chapter.
Various votive observances.

199.s:
agnir uvāca
ṛtuvratāntyahaṃ vakṣye bhuktimuktipradāni te /
indhanāni tu yo dadyādvarṣādicaturo hy ṛtūn //
199.d:
अग्निर् उवाच
ऋतुव्रतान्त्यहं वक्ष्ये भुक्तिमुक्तिप्रदानि ते /
इन्धनानि तु यो दद्याद्वर्षादिचतुरो ह्य् ऋतून् //
199.m:
Agni said:
I shall proclaim the seasonal votive observances that bestow worldly enjoyment and liberation upon you.
Whoever gives firewood during the four seasons beginning with the rainy season,

199.s:
ghṛtadhenupradaścānte brāhmaṇo 'gnivratī bhavet /
kṛtvā maunantu sandhyāyāṃ māsānte ghṛtakumbhadaḥ //
199.d:
घृतधेनुप्रदश्चान्ते ब्राह्मणो ऽग्निव्रती भवेत् /
कृत्वा मौनन्तु सन्ध्यायां मासान्ते घृतकुम्भदः //
199.m:
and at the end gives an effigy cow of ghee, is a Brahmin observing the vow of Agni.
Maintaining silence at twilight, and giving a jar of ghee at the end of the month,

199.s:
tilaghaṇṭāvastradātā sukhī sārasvatavratī(1) /
pañcāmṛtena snapanaṃ kṛtvābdaṃ dhenudo nṛpaḥ //
199.d:
तिलघण्टावस्त्रदाता सुखी सारस्वतव्रती(1) /
पञ्चामृतेन स्नपनं कृत्वाब्दं धेनुदो नृपः //
199.m:
and giving sesame seeds, a bell, and a garment, the observer of the Sārasvata vow becomes happy.
Bathing [the deity] with the five nectars and giving a cow for a year, one becomes a king.

199.s:
ekādaśyāntu naktāśī caitre bhaktaṃ nivedayet /
haimaṃ viṣṇoḥ padaṃ yāti māsante viṣṇusadvratī //
199.d:
एकादश्यान्तु नक्ताशी चैत्रे भक्तं निवेदयेत् /
हैमं विष्णोः पदं याति मासन्ते विष्णुसद्व्रती //
199.m:
Eating only at night on the eleventh lunar day, one should offer cooked food in Caitra;
at the end of the month, the true observer of Viṣṇu's vow goes to Viṣṇu’s golden abode.

199.s:
pāyasāśī goyugadaḥ śrībhāgdevīvratī bhavet /
nivedya pitṛdevebhyo yo bhuṅkte sa bhavennṛpaḥ //
199.d:
पायसाशी गोयुगदः श्रीभाग्देवीव्रती भवेत् /
निवेद्य पितृदेवेभ्यो यो भुङ्क्ते स भवेन्नृपः //
199.m:
Consuming milk pudding and giving a pair of cows, one shares in Śrī and becomes an observer of the goddess's vow.
One who eats only after offering to the ancestors and gods becomes a king.

199.s:
varṣavratāni coktāni(2) saṅkrāntivratakaṃ vade /
saṅkrāntau svargalokī syādrātrijāgaraṇānnaraḥ //
199.d:
वर्षव्रतानि चोक्तानि(2) सङ्क्रान्तिव्रतकं वदे /
सङ्क्रान्तौ स्वर्गलोकी स्याद्रात्रिजागरणान्नरः //
199.m:
The annual votive observances have been described; I shall tell of the solstice votive observance.
At a solstice, a person reaches the heavenly realm by keeping a night vigil.

199.s:
amāvāsyāṃ tu saṅkrāntau śivārkayajanāttathā /
uttare tvayane cājyaprasthasnānena keśave //
:n
1 sudhīḥ sārasvatavratī iti kha.. , ga.. , gha.. , cha.. , ṭa.. ca
2 sarvavratāni coktānīti kha.. , cha.. , ja.. ca
:p 235
199.d:
अमावास्यां तु सङ्क्रान्तौ शिवार्कयजनात्तथा /
उत्तरे त्वयने चाज्यप्रस्थस्नानेन केशवे //
:न्
1 सुधीः सारस्वतव्रती इति ख.. , ग.. , घ.. , छ.. , ट.. च
2 सर्वव्रतानि चोक्तानीति ख.. , छ.. , ज.. च
:प् 235
199.m:
And on a new moon day at a solstice, by worshipping Śiva and the Sun,
and at the northern solstice by bathing Keśava with a prastha of ghee,
[Footnote]
[Variant reading:] "sudhīḥ sārasvatavratī" in manuscripts kha, ga, gha, cha, and ṭa.
[Variant reading:] "sarvavratāni coktāni" in manuscripts kha, cha, and ja.

199.s:
dvātriṃśatpalamānena sarvapāpaiḥ pramucyate /
ghṛtakṣīrādinā snāpya prāpnoti viṣuvādiṣu //
199.d:
द्वात्रिंशत्पलमानेन सर्वपापैः प्रमुच्यते /
घृतक्षीरादिना स्नाप्य प्राप्नोति विषुवादिषु //
199.m:
measuring thirty-two palas, one is freed from all sins.
Bathing [him] with ghee, milk, and so on at equinoxes and similar occasions, one attains [the fruit].

199.s:
strīṇāmumāvrataṃ śrīdaṃ tṛtīyāsvaṣṭamīṣu ca /
gaurīṃ maheśvaraṃ cāpi yajet saubhāgyamāpnuyāt //
199.d:
स्त्रीणामुमाव्रतं श्रीदं तृतीयास्वष्टमीषु च /
गौरीं महेश्वरं चापि यजेत् सौभाग्यमाप्नुयात् //
199.m:
For women, the Umā-vow on the third and eighth lunar days bestows fortune.
One should worship Gaurī and Maheśvara; she will obtain good fortune in marriage.

199.s:
umāmaheśvarau prārcya aviyogādi cāpnuyāt /
mūlavratakarī strī ca umeśavratakāriṇī //
199.d:
उमामहेश्वरौ प्रार्च्य अवियोगादि चाप्नुयात् /
मूलव्रतकरी स्त्री च उमेशव्रतकारिणी //
199.m:
Having worshipped Umā and Maheśvara, a woman obtains non-separation [from her husband] and other blessings.
A woman observing the Mūla-vow or the vow of the Lord of Umā,

199.s:
sūryabhaktā tu yā nārī dhruvaṃ sā puruṣo bhavet /
:e ity āgneye mahāpurāṇe nānāvratāni nāma ekonaśatādhikaśatatamo
'dhyāyaḥ ||
:ś atha dviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
dīpadānavrataṃ
199.d:
सूर्यभक्ता तु या नारी ध्रुवं सा पुरुषो भवेत् /
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महापुराणे नानाव्रतानि नाम एकोनशताधिकशततमो
ऽध्यायः ||
:श् अथ द्विशततमो ऽध्यायः
दीपदानव्रतं
199.m:
or any woman devoted to the Sun, will surely become a man [in the next life].
Thus in the Great Purāṇa of Agni, the one hundred and ninety-ninth chapter, entitled ‘Various Votive Observances.’
Now begins the two-hundredth chapter.
The votive observance of giving lamps.

200.s:
agnnir uvāca
dīpadānavrataṃ vakṣye bhuktimuktipradāyakaṃ /
devadvijātikagṛhe dīpado 'bdaṃ sa sarvabhāk //
200.d:
अग्न्निर् उवाच
दीपदानव्रतं वक्ष्ये भुक्तिमुक्तिप्रदायकं /
देवद्विजातिकगृहे दीपदो ऽब्दं स सर्वभाक् //
200.m:
Agni said:
I shall explain the votive observance of giving lamps, which bestows worldly enjoyment and liberation.
One who gives a lamp in a temple of the gods or the house of a twice-born for a year enjoys everything.

200.s:
caturmāsaṃ viṣṇulokī kārttike svargalokyapi /
dīpadānāt paraṃ nāsti na bhūtaṃ na bhaviṣyati //
200.d:
चतुर्मासं विष्णुलोकी कार्त्तिके स्वर्गलोक्यपि /
दीपदानात् परं नास्ति न भूतं न भविष्यति //
200.m:
Giving it for four months, one goes to Viṣṇu’s realm; in Kārttika, one reaches the heavenly realm.
There is no gift superior to the gift of a lamp; none has been, nor will there ever be.

200.s:
dīpenāyuṣyacakṣuṣmāndīpāllakṣmīsutādikaṃ /
saubhāgyaṃ dīpadaḥ prāpya svargaloke nahīyate //
200.m:
Through the lamp, one obtains long life and eyesight; from the lamp comes Lakṣmī, sons, and more.
Having attained good fortune, the giver of a lamp does not fall from the heavenly realm.

Lalitā, the daughter of the king of Vidarbha, obtained her birth through the gift of a lamp.
[Page 236]
As the wife of King Cārudharman, she surpassed his hundred [other] wives.

200.s:
dadau dīpasahasraṃ sā viṣṇorāyatane satī /
pṛṣṭā sā dīpamāhātmyaṃ sapatnībhya uvāca ha //
lalitovāca
200.d:
ददौ दीपसहस्रं सा विष्णोरायतने सती /
पृष्टा सा दीपमाहात्म्यं सपत्नीभ्य उवाच ह //
ललितोवाच
200.m:
The chaste lady offered a thousand lamps in the temple of Viṣṇu.
Asked about the greatness of the lamp by her co-wives, she spoke:
Lalitā said:

200.s:
sauvīrarājasya purā maitreyo 'bhūt purohitaḥ /
tena cāyatanaṃ viṣṇoḥ kāritaṃ devikātaṭe //
200.d:
सौवीरराजस्य पुरा मैत्रेयो ऽभूत् पुरोहितः /
तेन चायतनं विष्णोः कारितं देविकातटे //
200.m:
Formerly, Maitreya was the royal priest of the king of Sauvīra;
by him a temple of Viṣṇu was built on the bank of the Devikā.

200.s:
kārttike dīpakastena dattaḥ samprerito mayā /
vaktraprāntena naśyantyā mārjārasya tadā bhayāt //
200.d:
कार्त्तिके दीपकस्तेन दत्तः सम्प्रेरितो मया /
वक्त्रप्रान्तेन नश्यन्त्या मार्जारस्य तदा भयात् //
200.m:
A lamp was offered there by him in Kārttika; then, fleeing in fear of a cat,
I, through the corner of my snout, trimmed it.

200.s:
nirvāṇavān pradīpto 'bhūdvartyā mūṣikayā tadā /
mṛtā rājātmajā jātā rājapatnī śatādhikā //
200.d:
निर्वाणवान् प्रदीप्तो ऽभूद्वर्त्या मूषिकया तदा /
मृता राजात्मजा जाता राजपत्नी शताधिका //
200.m:
Extinguished as it was, it was reignited by [my moving] the wick as a mouse then.
Having died, I was born as a king's daughter and became a queen surpassing a hundred wives.

200.s:
asaṅkalpitamapyasya preraṇaṃ yat kṛtaṃ mayā /
viṣṇāyatanadīpasya tasyedaṃ bhujyate phalaṃ //
200.d:
असङ्कल्पितमप्यस्य प्रेरणं यत् कृतं मया /
विष्णायतनदीपस्य तस्येदं भुज्यते फलं //
200.m:
Even though unintentioned, this fruit is enjoyed
from the trimming of the lamp in Viṣṇu's temple done by me.

200.s:
jātismarā hy ato dīpān prayacchāmi tvahar niśaṃ /
ekadaśyāṃ dīpado vai vimāne divi modate //
200.d:
जातिस्मरा ह्य् अतो दीपान् प्रयच्छामि त्वहर् निशं /
एकदश्यां दीपदो वै विमाने दिवि मोदते //
200.m:
Remembering my past lives, I therefore offer lamps day and night.
Indeed, one who gives a lamp on the eleventh lunar day rejoices in heaven in a celestial chariot.

200.s:
jāyate dīpahartā tu mūko vā jaḍa eva ca /
andhe tamasi duṣpāre narake patate kila //
200.d:
जायते दीपहर्ता तु मूको वा जड एव च /
अन्धे तमसि दुष्पारे नरके पतते किल //
200.m:
The stealer of a lamp is born either dumb or dull-witted,
and falls indeed into the blinding, impassable hell.

200.s:
vikrośamānāṃś ca narān yamakiṅkarāhatān /
vilāpair alamatrāpi kiṃ vo vilapite phalaṃ //
200.d:
विक्रोशमानांश् च नरान् यमकिङ्कराहतान् /
विलापैर् अलमत्रापि किं वो विलपिते फलं //
200.m:
And to the men crying out, beaten by the servants of Yama:
'Enough here of lamentations! What fruit is there in your wailing?

200.s:
yadā pramādibhiḥ pūrvamatyantasamupekṣitaḥ /
janturjanmasahasrebhyo hy ekasmin mānuṣo yadi //
200.d:
यदा प्रमादिभिः पूर्वमत्यन्तसमुपेक्षितः /
जन्तुर्जन्मसहस्रेभ्यो ह्य् एकस्मिन् मानुषो यदि //
200.m:
When formerly by the heedless [the soul] was utterly neglected,
if a creature from thousands of births becomes human in one,

200.s:
tatrāpyativimūḍhātmā kiṃ bhogānabhidhāvati /
svahitaṃ(1) viṣayāsvādaiḥ krandanaṃ tadihāgataṃ //
:n
1 harṣitamiti kha.. , ga.. , gha.. ca / dūṣitamiti ṅa..
:p 237
200.d:
तत्राप्यतिविमूढात्मा किं भोगानभिधावति /
स्वहितं(1) विषयास्वादैः क्रन्दनं तदिहागतं //
:न्
1 हर्षितमिति ख.. , ग.. , घ.. च / दूषितमिति ङ..
:प् 237
200.m:
even then, utterly deluded in mind, why does he pursue sensual pleasures?
[Abandoning] one's own welfare for tastes of sensory objects, that weeping has now arrived here.
[Footnote]
1. 'Delighted' in kha, ga, and gha; 'corrupted' in ṅa. / [Page 237]

200.s:
bhujyate ca kṛtaṃ pūrvametat kiṃ vo na cintitaṃ /
parastrīṣu kucābhyaṅgaṃ prītaye duḥkhadaṃ hi vaḥ //
200.d:
भुज्यते च कृतं पूर्वमेतत् किं वो न चिन्तितं /
परस्त्रीषु कुचाभ्यङ्गं प्रीतये दुःखदं हि वः //
200.m:
What was done previously is now experienced; did you not consider this?
Anointing the breasts of other men's wives for pleasure indeed brings you sorrow.

200.s:
muhūrtaviṣayāsvādo 'nekakoṭyavdaduḥkhadaḥ /
parastrīhāriyadgītaṃ hā mātaḥ kiṃ vilapyate //
200.d:
मुहूर्तविषयास्वादो ऽनेककोट्यव्ददुःखदः /
परस्त्रीहारियद्गीतं हा मातः किं विलप्यते //
200.m:
A momentary enjoyment of sense-objects brings sorrow for many millions of years.
Stealing other men's wives was celebrated; [now] why do you wail: 'Alas, mother!'?

200.s:
ko 'tibhāro harernāmni jihvayā parikīrtane /
vartitaile 'lpamūlye 'pi yadagnirlabhyate sadā //
200.d:
को ऽतिभारो हरेर्नाम्नि जिह्वया परिकीर्तने /
वर्तितैले ऽल्पमूल्ये ऽपि यदग्निर्लभ्यते सदा //
200.m:
What great burden is there in the name of Hari, in reciting it with the tongue?
Even when wick and oil are of little cost, because Agni is always obtained,

200.s:
dānāśaktair harerdīpo hṛtastadvo 'sti duḥkhadaṃ /
idānīṃ kiṃ vilāpena sahadhvaṃ yadupāgataṃ //
200.d:
दानाशक्तैर् हरेर्दीपो हृतस्तद्वो ऽस्ति दुःखदं /
इदानीं किं विलापेन सहध्वं यदुपागतं //
200.m:
Hari's lamp was stolen by those unable to give gifts; that brings you sorrow.
Now what is the use of lamentation? Endure what has arrived!'

200.s:
agnir uvāca
lalitoktañca tāḥ śrutvā dīpadānāddivaṃ yayuḥ /
tasmāddīpapradānena vratānāmadhikaṃ phalaṃ //
:e ity āgneye mahāpurāṇe dīpadānavrataṃ nāma dviśatatamo
'dhyāyaḥ ||
:ś athaikādhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
navavyūhārcanaṃ
200.d:
अग्निर् उवाच
ललितोक्तञ्च ताः श्रुत्वा दीपदानाद्दिवं ययुः /
तस्माद्दीपप्रदानेन व्रतानामधिकं फलं //
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महापुराणे दीपदानव्रतं नाम द्विशततमो
ऽध्यायः ||
:श् अथैकाधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः
नवव्यूहार्चनं
200.m:
Agni said:
And having heard what was spoken by Lalitā, they went to heaven through the gift of lamps;
therefore, greater fruit of votive observances comes through the offering of lamps.
Thus ends the two-hundredth chapter, named the Votive Observance of the Gift of Lamps, in the Great Agni Purāṇa.
Now, the two hundred and first chapter.
Worship of the Nine Emanations.

201.s:
agnir uvāca
navavyūhārcanaṃ vakṣye nāradāya harīritaṃ /
maṇḍale 'bje 'rcayenmadhye avījaṃ vāsudevakaṃ //
201.d:
अग्निर् उवाच
नवव्यूहार्चनं वक्ष्ये नारदाय हरीरितं /
मण्डले ऽब्जे ऽर्चयेन्मध्ये अवीजं वासुदेवकं //
201.m:
Agni said:
I shall explain the worship of the nine emanations, as told by Hari to Nārada.
In the lotus of the maṇḍala, in the center, one should worship Vāsudeva with the seed-syllable 'A'.

201.s:
āvījañca saṅkarṣaṇam pradyumnaṃ ca dakṣiṇe /
:p 238
aḥ anuruddhaṃ naiṛte oṃ nārāyaṇamapsu ca //
201.d:
आवीजञ्च सङ्कर्षणम् प्रद्युम्नं च दक्षिणे /
:प् 238
अः अनुरुद्धं नैऋते ओं नारायणमप्सु च //

201.s:
tat sadbrahmāṇamanile huṃ viṣṇuṃ kṣauṃ nṛsiṃhakaṃ(1) /
uttare bhūrvarāhañca īśe dvāri ca paścime //
201.d:
तत् सद्ब्रह्माणमनिले हुं विष्णुं क्षौं नृसिंहकं(1) /
उत्तरे भूर्वराहञ्च ईशे द्वारि च पश्चिमे //
201.m:
Brahmā with 'Tat Sat' in the wind [quarter, the northwest], Viṣṇu with 'Huṃ', Nṛsiṃha with 'Kṣauṃ',
Bhūvarāha in the north, and in the northeast and the western gate;

201.s:
kaṃ ṭaṃ saṃ śaṃ garutmantaṃ pūrvavaktrañca dakṣiṇe(2) /
khaṃ chaṃ vaṃ huṃ phaḍiti ca khaṃ ṭhaṃ phaṃ śaṃ gadāṃvidhau //
201.d:
कं टं सं शं गरुत्मन्तं पूर्ववक्त्रञ्च दक्षिणे(2) /
खं छं वं हुं फडिति च खं ठं फं शं गदांविधौ //
201.m:
one should worship Garuḍa with 'Kaṃ Ṭaṃ Saṃ Śaṃ', facing east in the south,
and with 'Khaṃ Chaṃ Vaṃ Huṃ Phaṭ' and 'Khaṃ Ṭhaṃ Phaṃ Śaṃ' the club in the north;

201.s:
baṃ ṇaṃ maṃ kṣaṃ koṇeśañca ghaṃ daṃ bhaṃ haṃśriyaṃ yajet /
dakṣiṇe cottare puṣṭiṃ gaṃ ḍaṃ baṃ śaṃ svavījakaṃ //
201.d:
बं णं मं क्षं कोणेशञ्च घं दं भं हंश्रियं यजेत् /
दक्षिणे चोत्तरे पुष्टिं गं डं बं शं स्ववीजकं //
201.m:
and the lord of the corner with 'Baṃ Ṇaṃ Maṃ Kṣaṃ', and Śrī with 'Ghaṃ Daṃ Bhaṃ Haṃ';
in the south, and Puṣṭi in the north with her own seed-syllables 'Gaṃ Ḍaṃ Baṃ Śaṃ';

201.s:
pīṭhasya paścime dhaṃ vaṃ vanamālāñca paścime /
śrīvatsaṃ caiva saṃ haṃ laṃ chaṃ taṃ yaṃ kaustubhaṃ jale //
201.d:
पीठस्य पश्चिमे धं वं वनमालाञ्च पश्चिमे /
श्रीवत्सं चैव सं हं लं छं तं यं कौस्तुभं जले //
201.m:
to the west of the pedestal with 'Dhaṃ Vaṃ', and the garland of forest flowers in the west;
and the Śrīvatsa with 'Saṃ Haṃ Laṃ', and Kaustubha in the water [quarter] with 'Chaṃ Taṃ Yaṃ'.

201.d:
दशमाङ्गक्रमाद्विष्णोर्नमो ऽनन्तमधो ऽर्चयेत् /
दशाङ्गादिमहेन्द्रादीन् पूर्वादौ चतुरो घटान् //
201.m:
In the order of the ten limbs of Viṣṇu, one should worship with 'Namah' Ananta below;
the great Indras and others beginning with the ten limbs, [and] four water-jars beginning in the east;

201.s:
toraṇāni vitānaṃ ca agnyanilenduvījakaiḥ /
maṇḍalāni kramāddhyātvā tanuṃ vandya tataḥ plavet //
201.d:
तोरणानि वितानं च अग्न्यनिलेन्दुवीजकैः /
मण्डलानि क्रमाद्ध्यात्वा तनुं वन्द्य ततः प्लवेत् //
201.m:
arched gateways, a canopy, and, having meditated in sequence on the maṇḍalas
with the seed-syllables of fire, wind, and the moon, having saluted the body, one should then flood [it].

201.s:
amvarasthaṃ tato dhyātvā sūkṣmarūpamathātmanaḥ /
sitāmṛte nimagnañca(3) candravimvāt srutena ca //
201.d:
अम्वरस्थं ततो ध्यात्वा सूक्ष्मरूपमथात्मनः /
सितामृते निमग्नञ्च(3) चन्द्रविम्वात् स्रुतेन च //
201.m:
Then, having meditated on one's own subtle form situated in the sky,
immersed in white nectar flowing from the disc of the moon,

201.s:
tadeva cātmano vījamamṛtaṃ plavasaṃskṛtaṃ /
utpādyamānaṃ puruṣamātmānamupakalpayet //
201.d:
तदेव चात्मनो वीजममृतं प्लवसंस्कृतं /
उत्पाद्यमानं पुरुषमात्मानमुपकल्पयेत् //
201.m:
and that very nectar-seed of one's own self, purified by flooding,
one should imagine oneself as the Person being brought into being.

201.s:
utpanno 'smi svayaṃ viṣṇurvījaṃ dvādaśakaṃ nyaset /
hṛcchirastu śikhā caiva kavacaṃ cāstrameva ca //
201.d:
उत्पन्नो ऽस्मि स्वयं विष्णुर्वीजं द्वादशकं न्यसेत् /
हृच्छिरस्तु शिखा चैव कवचं चास्त्रमेव च //
201.m:
'I am born as Viṣṇu himself'—one should deposit the twelve seed-syllables:
the heart, the head, the crest, the armor, and the weapon,

201.s:
vakṣomūrdhaśikhāpṛṣṭhalocaneṣu nyaseta punaḥ /
astraṃ karadvaye nyasya tato divyatanurbhavet //
:n
1 krūṃ viṣṇuṃ kṣauṃ nṛsiṃhakamiti kha.. , cha.. , ja.. ca
2 pakṣirājañca dakṣiṇe iti ṅa..
3 sitāsite nimagnañceti kha.. , ja.. ca
:p 239
201.d:
वक्षोमूर्धशिखापृष्ठलोचनेषु न्यसेत पुनः /
अस्त्रं करद्वये न्यस्य ततो दिव्यतनुर्भवेत् //
:न्
1 क्रूं विष्णुं क्षौं नृसिंहकमिति ख.. , छ.. , ज.. च
2 पक्षिराजञ्च दक्षिणे इति ङ..
3 सितासिते निमग्नञ्चेति ख.. , ज.. च
:प् 239
201.m:
one should deposit again on the chest, crown, crest, back, and eyes;
having deposited the weapon on both hands, one then becomes of divine body.
[Note]
1. Manuscripts kha, cha, and ja read: "krūṃ to Viṣṇu, kṣauṃ to Nṛsiṃha".
2. Manuscript ṅa reads: "and the king of birds in the south".
3. Manuscripts kha and ja read: "plunged in the white and dark [waters]".
[Page 239]

201.s:
yathātmani tathā deve śiṣyadehe nyasettathā /
anirmālyā smṛtā pūjā yaddhareḥ pūjanaṃ hṛdi //
201.d:
यथात्मनि तथा देवे शिष्यदेहे न्यसेत्तथा /
अनिर्माल्या स्मृता पूजा यद्धरेः पूजनं हृदि //
201.m:
As upon oneself, so upon the deity, and likewise one should deposit upon the body of the disciple.
The worship of Hari in the heart is traditionally considered free of remnant flowers;

201.s:
sanirmālyā maṇḍalādau baddhanetrāś ca śiṣyakāḥ /
puṣpaṃ kṣipeyuryanmūrtau tasya tannāma kārayet //
201.d:
सनिर्माल्या मण्डलादौ बद्धनेत्राश् च शिष्यकाः /
पुष्पं क्षिपेयुर्यन्मूर्तौ तस्य तन्नाम कारयेत् //
201.m:
accompanied by remnant flowers in the maṇḍala and so forth. With blindfolded eyes, the disciples
should cast a flower; on whichever icon [it falls], he should assign him that name.

201.s:
niveśya vāmataḥ śiṣyāṃstilavrīhighṛtaṃ hunet /
śatamaṣṭottaraṃ hutvā sahasraṃ kāyaśuddhaye //
201.d:
निवेश्य वामतः शिष्यांस्तिलव्रीहिघृतं हुनेत् /
शतमष्टोत्तरं हुत्वा सहस्रं कायशुद्धये //
201.m:
Having seated the disciples to the left, he should offer sesame, rice, and ghee in the fire;
having offered one hundred and eight [oblations], or a thousand for the purification of the body,

201.s:
navavyūhasya mūrtīnāmaṅgānāṃ ca śatādhikaṃ /
pūṛṇāndattvā dīkṣayettān guruḥ pūjyaś ca tair dhanaiḥ //
:e ity āgneye mahāpurāṇe navavyūhārcanaṃ nāma
ekādhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
:ś atha dvyadhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
puṣpādhyāyakathanaṃ
201.d:
नवव्यूहस्य मूर्तीनामङ्गानां च शताधिकं /
पूऋणान्दत्त्वा दीक्षयेत्तान् गुरुः पूज्यश् च तैर् धनैः //
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महापुराणे नवव्यूहार्चनं नाम
एकाधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः ||
:श् अथ द्व्यधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः
पुष्पाध्यायकथनं
201.m:
and more than a hundred for the icons and limbs of the nine emanations,
having given the full oblation, he should initiate them; and the guru should be honored by them with wealth.
Thus ends the two hundred and first chapter, named the Worship of the Nine Emanations, in the Great Agni Purāṇa.
Now, the two hundred and second chapter.
Discourse on the Chapter on Flowers.

202.s:
agnir uvāca
puṣpagandhadhūpadīpanaivedyaistuṣyate hariḥ /
puṣpāṇi devayogyāni hy ayogyāni vadāmi te //
202.d:
अग्निर् उवाच
पुष्पगन्धधूपदीपनैवेद्यैस्तुष्यते हरिः /
पुष्पाणि देवयोग्यानि ह्य् अयोग्यानि वदामि ते //
202.m:
Agni said:
Hari is pleased by flowers, fragrant scents, incense, lamps, and food offerings.
I will tell you the flowers suitable for the gods and those unsuitable.

202.s:
puṣpaṃ śreṣṭhaṃ mālatī ca tamālo bhuktimuktimān /
mallikā sarvapāpaghnī yūthikā viṣṇulokadā //
202.d:
पुष्पं श्रेष्ठं मालती च तमालो भुक्तिमुक्तिमान् /
मल्लिका सर्वपापघ्नी यूथिका विष्णुलोकदा //
202.m:
Mālatī is an excellent flower; tamāla brings worldly enjoyment and liberation;
mallikā destroys all sins; yūthikā grants the realm of Viṣṇu;

202.s:
atimuktamayaṃ tadvat pāṭalā viṣṇulokadā /
:p 240
karavīrair viṣṇulokī javāpuṣpaiś ca puṇyavān //
202.d:
अतिमुक्तमयं तद्वत् पाटला विष्णुलोकदा /
:प् 240
करवीरैर् विष्णुलोकी जवापुष्पैश् च पुण्यवान् //

202.s:
pāvantīkubjakādyaiś ca tagarair viṣṇulokabhāk /
karṇikārair viṣṇulokaḥ karuṇṭhaiḥ pāpanāśanaṃ //
202.d:
पावन्तीकुब्जकाद्यैश् च तगरैर् विष्णुलोकभाक् /
कर्णिकारैर् विष्णुलोकः करुण्ठैः पापनाशनं //
202.m:
with pāvantī, kubjaka, and others, and with tagara flowers, one attains the realm of Viṣṇu;
with karṇikāra flowers the realm of Viṣṇu is attained; with karuṇṭha flowers sins are destroyed;

202.s:
padmaiś ca ketakībhiś ca kundapuṣpaiḥ parā gatiḥ /
vāṇapuṣpair varvarābhiḥ kṛṣṇābhirharilokabhāk //
202.d:
पद्मैश् च केतकीभिश् च कुन्दपुष्पैः परा गतिः /
वाणपुष्पैर् वर्वराभिः कृष्णाभिर्हरिलोकभाक् //
202.m:
and with padmas, ketakīs, and kunda flowers the highest state [is reached];
with vāṇa flowers, varvarās, and kṛṣṇās, one attains the realm of Hari;

202.s:
aśokaistilakaistadvadaṭarūṣabhavais tathā /
muktibhāgī bilvapatraiḥ śamīpatraiḥ parā gatiḥ //
202.d:
अशोकैस्तिलकैस्तद्वदटरूषभवैस् तथा /
मुक्तिभागी बिल्वपत्रैः शमीपत्रैः परा गतिः //
202.m:
likewise with aśokas, tilakas, and flowers produced from aṭarūṣa;
one shares liberation through bilva leaves; through śamī leaves, the highest state [is attained];

202.s:
viṣṇulokī bhṛṅgarājaistamālasya dalais tathā /
tulasī kṛṣṇagaurākhyā kalhārotpalakāni ca //
202.d:
विष्णुलोकी भृङ्गराजैस्तमालस्य दलैस् तथा /
तुलसी कृष्णगौराख्या कल्हारोत्पलकानि च //
202.m:
one attains the realm of Viṣṇu with bhṛṅgarāja and leaves of tamāla;
with tulasī called dark and pale, and kalhāra and utpala lotuses,

202.s:
padmaṃ kokanadaṃ puṇyaṃ śatābjamālayā hariḥ /
nīpārjunakadambaiś ca(1) vakulaiś ca sugandhibhiḥ //
202.d:
पद्मं कोकनदं पुण्यं शताब्जमालया हरिः /
नीपार्जुनकदम्बैश् च(1) वकुलैश् च सुगन्धिभिः //
202.m:
meritorious white padma and red water-lily, with a garland of a hundred lotuses Hari [is pleased];
and with fragrant blossoms of nīpa, arjuna, kadamba, and vakula;

202.s:
kiṃśukair munipuṣpaistu gokarṇair nāgakarṇakaiḥ /
sandhyāpuṣpair bilvatakai rañjanīketakībhavaiḥ(2) //
202.d:
किंशुकैर् मुनिपुष्पैस्तु गोकर्णैर् नागकर्णकैः /
सन्ध्यापुष्पैर् बिल्वतकै रञ्जनीकेतकीभवैः(2) //
202.m:
with kiṃśukas, munipuṣpas, gokarṇas, and nāgakarṇas,
with sandhyāpuṣpas, bilvatakas, and those born of rañjanī and ketakī;

202.s:
kuṣmāṇḍatimirotthaiś ca kuśakāśaśarodbhavaiḥ /
dyūtādibhirmaruvakaiḥ patrairanyaiḥ sugandhikaiḥ //
202.d:
कुष्माण्डतिमिरोत्थैश् च कुशकाशशरोद्भवैः /
द्यूतादिभिर्मरुवकैः पत्रैरन्यैः सुगन्धिकैः //
202.m:
with those from pumpkin, timira, and those born of kuśa, kāśa, and śara grass,
with maruvaka, dyūta, and others, and with other fragrant leaves.

202.s:
bhuktimuktiḥ pāpahānirbhaktyā sarvaistu tuṣyati /
svarṇalakṣādhikaṃ puṣpaṃ mālā koṭiguṇādhikā //
202.d:
भुक्तिमुक्तिः पापहानिर्भक्त्या सर्वैस्तु तुष्यति /
स्वर्णलक्षाधिकं पुष्पं माला कोटिगुणाधिका //
202.m:
Worldly enjoyment, liberation, and destruction of sins [occur]; he is pleased with all through devotion.
A flower is greater than a hundred thousand [measures of] gold; a garland is a ten-million-fold greater.

202.s:
svavane 'nyavane puṣpaistriguṇaṃ vanajaiḥ phalaṃ(3) /
viśīrṇairnārcayedviṣṇunnādhikāṅgairna moṭitaiḥ //
202.d:
स्ववने ऽन्यवने पुष्पैस्त्रिगुणं वनजैः फलं(3) /
विशीर्णैर्नार्चयेद्विष्णुन्नाधिकाङ्गैर्न मोटितैः //
202.m:
With flowers from one's own forest or another's forest, three-fold fruit [is attained] through forest-grown ones.
One must not worship Viṣṇu with withered, malformed, or broken [flowers],

202.s:
kāñcanāraistathonmattairgirikarṇikayā tathā /
:n
1 muktibhāgo kadambaiśceti ṅa..
2 rajanīketakībhavairiti kha.. , ṅa.. , cha.. , ja.. ca
3 jalajaiḥ phalamiti ṅa..
:p 241
kuṭajaiḥ śālmalīyaiś ca(1) śirīṣair narakādikaṃ //
202.d:
काञ्चनारैस्तथोन्मत्तैर्गिरिकर्णिकया तथा /
:न्
1 मुक्तिभागो कदम्बैश्चेति ङ..
2 रजनीकेतकीभवैरिति ख.. , ङ.. , छ.. , ज.. च
3 जलजैः फलमिति ङ..
:प् 241
कुटजैः शाल्मलीयैश् च(1) शिरीषैर् नरकादिकं //
202.m:
nor with kāñcanāra, unmatta, or girikarṇikā;
[Note]
1. Manuscript ṅa reads: "partaking of liberation with kadamba flowers".
2. Manuscripts kha, ṅa, cha, and ja read: "with those born of night and ketakī flowers".
3. Manuscript ṅa reads: "the fruit with water-born [flowers]".
[Page 241]
[Offerings of] kuṭaja, silk-cotton and śirīṣa flowers lead to hell and the like.

202.s:
sugandhairbrahmapadmaiś ca(2) puṣpairnīlotpalairhariḥ(3) /
arkamandāradhustūrakusumairarcyate haraḥ //
202.d:
सुगन्धैर्ब्रह्मपद्मैश् च(2) पुष्पैर्नीलोत्पलैर्हरिः(3) /
अर्कमन्दारधुस्तूरकुसुमैरर्च्यते हरः //
202.m: Hari is worshipped with fragrant brahmapadma blossoms and blue lotuses; / Hara is worshipped with flowers of arka, mandāra, and dhattūra.

202.s:
kuṭajaiḥ karkaṭīpuṣpaiḥ ketakīnna śive dadet /
kuṣmāṇḍanimbasambhūtaṃ paiśācaṃ gandhavarjitaṃ //
202.d:
कुटजैः कर्कटीपुष्पैः केतकीन्न शिवे ददेत् /
कुष्माण्डनिम्बसम्भूतं पैशाचं गन्धवर्जितं //
202.m: One should not offer kuṭaja flowers, karkaṭī blossoms, or ketakī to Śiva; / [nor] what is produced from pumpkins and nīm, nor what belongs to Piśācas or is devoid of fragrance.

202.s:
ahiṃsā indriyajayaḥ(4) kṣāntirjñānaṃ(5) dayā śrutaṃ /
bhāvāṣtapuṣpaiḥ sampūjya devān syād bhuktimuktibhāk //
202.d:
अहिंसा इन्द्रियजयः(4) क्षान्तिर्ज्ञानं(5) दया श्रुतं /
भावाष्तपुष्पैः सम्पूज्य देवान् स्याद् भुक्तिमुक्तिभाक् //
202.m: Non-violence, mastery of the senses, patience, knowledge, compassion, and sacred learning— / worshipping the gods with [these] eight mental flowers, one attains worldly enjoyment and liberation.

202.s:
ahiṃsā prathamaṃ puṣpaṃ puṣpamindriyanigrahaḥ /
sarvapuṣpaṃ dayā bhūte puṣpaṃ śāntirviśiṣyate //
202.d:
अहिंसा प्रथमं पुष्पं पुष्पमिन्द्रियनिग्रहः /
सर्वपुष्पं दया भूते पुष्पं शान्तिर्विशिष्यते //
202.m: Non-violence is the first flower; restraint of the senses is a flower; / compassion towards living beings is the all-flower; peace is considered an excellent flower;

202.s:
śamaḥ puṣpaṃ tapaḥ puṣpaṃ dhyānaṃ puṣpaṃ casaptamaṃ /
satyañcaivāṣṭamaṃ puṣpametaistuṣyati keśavaḥ //
202.d:
शमः पुष्पं तपः पुष्पं ध्यानं पुष्पं चसप्तमं /
सत्यञ्चैवाष्टमं पुष्पमेतैस्तुष्यति केशवः //
202.m: tranquillity is a flower; ascetic austerity is a flower; meditation is the seventh flower; / and truth is the eighth flower: Keśava is pleased with these.

202.s:
etairevāṣṭabhiḥ puṣpaistuṣyatyevārcito hariḥ /
puṣpāntarāṇi santyatra vāhyāni manujottama //
202.d:
एतैरेवाष्टभिः पुष्पैस्तुष्यत्येवार्चितो हरिः /
पुष्पान्तराणि सन्त्यत्र वाह्यानि मनुजोत्तम //
202.m: Hari, when worshipped with these eight flowers alone, is indeed pleased. / There are other flowers here that are external, O best of men:

202.s:
bhaktyā dayānvitairviṣṇuḥ pūjitaḥ parituṣyati(6) /
vāruṇaṃ salilaṃ puṣpaṃ saumyaṃ ghṛtapayodadhi //
202.d:
भक्त्या दयान्वितैर्विष्णुः पूजितः परितुष्यति(6) /
वारुणं सलिलं पुष्पं सौम्यं घृतपयोदधि //
202.m: Viṣṇu is fully pleased when worshipped with devotion by those endowed with compassion. / Water is the flower belonging to Varuṇa; ghee, milk, and curd belong to Soma;

202.s:
prājāpatyaṃ tathānnādi āgneyaṃ dhūpadīpakaṃ /
phalapuṣpādikañcaiva vānaspatyantu pañcamaṃ //
202.d:
प्राजापत्यं तथान्नादि आग्नेयं धूपदीपकं /
फलपुष्पादिकञ्चैव वानस्पत्यन्तु पञ्चमं //
202.m: grain and the like belong to Prajāpati; incense and lamps belong to Agni; / and fruits, flowers, and the like are the fifth, belonging to forest trees;

202.s:
pārthivaṃ kuśamūlādyaṃ vāyavyaṃ gandhacandanaṃ /
:n
1 śālmalijaiśceti kha.. , ga.. , ṅa.. ca
2 sugandhaiḥ patrapuṣpaiśceti ṅa..
3 pūjyo nīlotpalairhaririti kha.. , ga.. , ṅa.. , ja.. ca
4 ahiṃsā indriyayayama iti ga..
5 kṣāntirdānamiti kha..
6 ahiṃsā prathamaṃ puṣpamityādiḥ, pūjitaḥ parituṣyati ity
antaḥ pāṭhaḥ kha.. , ga.. , gha.. , ṅa.. , cha.. , ja.. , ña.. , ṭa..
pustakeṣu nāsti
:p 242
śraddhākhyaṃ viṣṇupuṣpañca sarvadā cāṣṭapuṣpikāḥ //
202.d:
पार्थिवं कुशमूलाद्यं वायव्यं गन्धचन्दनं /
:न्
1 शाल्मलिजैश्चेति ख.. , ग.. , ङ.. च
2 सुगन्धैः पत्रपुष्पैश्चेति ङ..
3 पूज्यो नीलोत्पलैर्हरिरिति ख.. , ग.. , ङ.. , ज.. च
4 अहिंसा इन्द्रियययम इति ग..
5 क्षान्तिर्दानमिति ख..
6 अहिंसा प्रथमं पुष्पमित्यादिः, पूजितः परितुष्यति इत्य्
अन्तः पाठः ख.. , ग.. , घ.. , ङ.. , छ.. , ज.. , ञ.. , ट..
पुस्तकेषु नास्ति
:प् 242
श्रद्धाख्यं विष्णुपुष्पञ्च सर्वदा चाष्टपुष्पिकाः //
202.m:
kuśa grass, roots, and the like belong to the earth; perfume and sandalwood belong to Vāyu.
[Note]
1. 'śālmalijaiś ceti' in manuscripts kha, ga, and ṅa.
2. 'sugandhaiḥ patrapuṣpaiś ceti' in manuscript ṅa.
3. 'pūjyo nīlotpalair harir iti' in manuscripts kha, ga, ṅa, and ja.
4. 'ahiṃsā indriyayama iti' in manuscript ga.
5. 'kṣāntir dānam iti' in manuscript kha.
6. The reading beginning with 'ahiṃsā prathamaṃ puṣpam' up to 'pūjitaḥ parituṣyati' is absent in manuscripts kha, ga, gha, ṅa, cha, ja, ña, and ṭa.
The flower of Viṣṇu named faith and the constant eightfold flowers [are offered].

202.s:
āsanaṃ mūrtipañcāṅgaṃ(1) viṣṇurvā cāṣṭapuṣpikāḥ /
viṣṇostu vāsudevādyairīśānādyaiḥ śivasya vā //
:e ity āgneye mahāpurāṇe puṣpādhyāyo nāma dvyadhikadviśatatamo
'dhyāyaḥ ||
:ś atha tryadhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
narakasvarūpam
202.d:
आसनं मूर्तिपञ्चाङ्गं(1) विष्णुर्वा चाष्टपुष्पिकाः /
विष्णोस्तु वासुदेवाद्यैरीशानाद्यैः शिवस्य वा //
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महापुराणे पुष्पाध्यायो नाम द्व्यधिकद्विशततमो
ऽध्यायः ||
:श् अथ त्र्यधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः
नरकस्वरूपम्
202.m:
The seat, the five parts of the icon, or Viṣṇu [himself], with the eightfold flowers; / of Viṣṇu, with [the mantras of] Vāsudeva and others, or of Śiva, with those of Īśāna and others.
Thus in the Agni Mahāpurāṇa, the two hundred and second chapter, entitled 'The Chapter on Flowers'.
Now, the two hundred and third chapter:
The Nature of Hells.

203.s:
agnir uvāca
puṣpādyaiḥ pūjanādviṣṇor na yāti narakāndave /
āyuṣo 'nte naraḥ prāṇairanicchannapi mucyate //
203.d:
अग्निर् उवाच
पुष्पाद्यैः पूजनाद्विष्णोर् न याति नरकान्दवे /
आयुषो ऽन्ते नरः प्राणैरनिच्छन्नपि मुच्यते //
203.m: Agni said: / By worshipping Viṣṇu with flowers and other offerings, a man does not go to the blinding hells. / At the end of his lifespan, he is released from his vital breaths even against his will.

203.s:
jalamagnirviṣaṃ śastraṃ kṣudvyādhiḥ patanaṃ gireḥ /
nimittaṃ kiñcidāsādya dehī prāṇairvimucyate //
203.d:
जलमग्निर्विषं शस्त्रं क्षुद्व्याधिः पतनं गिरेः /
निमित्तं किञ्चिदासाद्य देही प्राणैर्विमुच्यते //
203.m: Water, fire, poison, weapons, hunger, disease, or falling from a mountain— / having met with some such cause, the embodied soul is released from its vital breaths.

203.s:
anyaccharīramādatte yātanīyaṃ svakarmabhiḥ /
bhuṅkte 'tha pāpakṛt duḥkhaṃ sukhaṃ dharmāya saṅgataḥ //
203.d:
अन्यच्छरीरमादत्ते यातनीयं स्वकर्मभिः /
भुङ्क्ते ऽथ पापकृत् दुःखं सुखं धर्माय सङ्गतः //
203.m: It takes on another body meant for suffering, in accordance with its own deeds; / then the evildoer experiences sorrow, while one devoted to righteousness experiences happiness.

203.s:
nīyate yamadūtaistu yamaṃ prāṇibhayaṅkaraiḥ /
kupathe dakṣiṇadvāri dharmikaḥ paścimādibhiḥ //
203.d:
नीयते यमदूतैस्तु यमं प्राणिभयङ्करैः /
कुपथे दक्षिणद्वारि धर्मिकः पश्चिमादिभिः //
203.m: He is led to Yama by Yama's messengers, who terrify living beings— / on a bad path through the southern gate, whereas the righteous man goes through the western and other [gates].

203.s:
yamājñaptaiḥ kiṅkaraistu pātyate narakeṣu ca(2) /
:n
1 āsanaṃ mūrtiṣoḍhāṅgamiti kha..
2 pātyate narakeṣvapi iti kha.. / pātyate narake sadā iti ṅa.. /pīḍyate
narake 'dhuneti gha.. , cha.. ca
:p 243
svarge tu nīyate dharmād vasiṣṭhādyuktisaṃśrayāt //
203.d:
यमाज्ञप्तैः किङ्करैस्तु पात्यते नरकेषु च(2) /
:न्
1 आसनं मूर्तिषोढाङ्गमिति ख..
2 पात्यते नरकेष्वपि इति ख.. / पात्यते नरके सदा इति ङ.. /पीड्यते
नरके ऽधुनेति घ.. , छ.. च
:प् 243
स्वर्गे तु नीयते धर्माद् वसिष्ठाद्युक्तिसंश्रयात् //
203.m:
He is cast into the hells by the servants commanded by Yama.
[Note]
1. 'āsanaṃ mūrtiṣoḍhāṅgam iti' in manuscript kha.
2. 'pātyate narakeṣv api iti' in manuscript kha; 'pātyate narake sadā iti' in manuscript ṅa; 'pīḍyate narake 'dhunā iti' in manuscripts gha and cha.
To heaven, however, one is led through righteousness by taking refuge in the teachings of Vasiṣṭha and others.

203.s:
goghātī tu mahāvīcyāṃ varṣalakṣantu pīḍyate /
āmakumbhe mahādīpte brahmahā bhūmihārakaḥ //
203.d:
गोघाती तु महावीच्यां वर्षलक्षन्तु पीड्यते /
आमकुम्भे महादीप्ते ब्रह्महा भूमिहारकः //
203.m: The cow-killer is tormented in Mahāvīci for a hundred thousand years; / in Āmakumbha, glowing with intense heat, the slayer of a brahmin and the stealer of land [are tormented];

203.s:
mahāpralayakaṃ yāvadraurave pīḍyate śanaiḥ /
strībālavṛddhahantā tu yāvadindrāś caturdaśa //
203.d:
महाप्रलयकं यावद्रौरवे पीड्यते शनैः /
स्त्रीबालवृद्धहन्ता तु यावदिन्द्राश् चतुर्दश //
203.m: until the great cosmic dissolution he is tormented slowly in Raurava; / while the killer of women, children, and the elderly [is tormented] for the span of fourteen Indras.

203.s:
mahārauravake raudre gṛhakṣetrādidīpakaḥ /
dahyate kalpamekaṃ sa caurastāmisrake patet //
203.d:
महारौरवके रौद्रे गृहक्षेत्रादिदीपकः /
दह्यते कल्पमेकं स चौरस्तामिस्रके पतेत् //
203.m: In fierce Mahāraurava, he who burns houses, fields, and the like / is burnt for one aeon; a thief falls into Tāmisra.

203.s:
naikakalpantu śūlādyairbhidyate yamakiṅkaraiḥ /
mahātāmisrake sarpajalaukādyaiś ca pīḍyate //
203.d:
नैककल्पन्तु शूलाद्यैर्भिद्यते यमकिङ्करैः /
महातामिस्रके सर्पजलौकाद्यैश् च पीड्यते //
203.m: For many aeons he is pierced with tridents and other weapons by Yama's servants; / in Mahātāmisra, he is tormented by snakes, leeches, and the like.

203.s:
yāvadbhūmirmātṛhādyā asipatravane 'sibhiḥ(1) /
naikakalpantu narake karambhavālukāsu ca //
203.d:
यावद्भूमिर्मातृहाद्या असिपत्रवने ऽसिभिः(1) /
नैककल्पन्तु नरके करम्भवालुकासु च //
203.m: The killer of a mother and the like [are tormented] with swords in Asipatravana for as long as the earth exists, / and for many aeons in the hell of Karambhavālukā.

203.s:
yena dagdho janastatra dahyate vālukādibhiḥ /
kākole kṛmiviṣṭhāśī ekākī miṣṭabhojanaḥ //
203.d:
येन दग्धो जनस्तत्र दह्यते वालुकादिभिः /
काकोले कृमिविष्ठाशी एकाकी मिष्टभोजनः //
203.m: He by whom a person was burnt is burnt there by burning sands and the like. / In Kākola, one who eats sweets alone eats worms and excrement.

203.s:
kuṭṭale mūtraraktāśī pañcayajñakriyojjhitaḥ /
sudurgandhe raktabhojī bhaveccābhakṣyabhakṣyakaḥ //
203.d:
कुट्टले मूत्ररक्ताशी पञ्चयज्ञक्रियोज्झितः /
सुदुर्गन्धे रक्तभोजी भवेच्चाभक्ष्यभक्ष्यकः //
203.m: In Kuṭṭala, one who abandoned the rites of the five great sacrifices consumes urine and blood; / in Sudurgandha, one who eats what is forbidden to be eaten becomes a consumer of blood.

203.s:
tailapāke tu tilavat pīḍyate parapīḍakaḥ /
tailapāke tu pacyeta śaraṇāgataghātakaḥ //
203.d:
तैलपाके तु तिलवत् पीड्यते परपीडकः /
तैलपाके तु पच्येत शरणागतघातकः //
203.m: In Tailapāka, a tormentor of others is crushed like sesame seeds; / and in Tailapāka, the killer of one who has sought refuge is cooked.

203.s:
nirucchāse dānanāśī rasavikrayako 'dhvare /
nāmnā vajrakavāṭena mahāpāte tadānṛtī //
203.d:
निरुच्छासे दाननाशी रसविक्रयको ऽध्वरे /
नाम्ना वज्रकवाटेन महापाते तदानृती //
203.m: In Nirucchāsa, one who destroys gifts and one who sells liquids during a sacrifice [are punished]; / in the great pit named Vajrakavāṭa, a liar is then punished.

203.s:
mahājvāle pāpabuddhiḥ krakace 'gamyagāminaḥ /
saṅkarī guḍapāke ca(2) pratudet paramarmanut //
:n
1 asipatravane 'gnibhiriti ṅa..
2 gurupāke ceti kha.. , ja.. ca
:p 244
203.d:
महाज्वाले पापबुद्धिः क्रकचे ऽगम्यगामिनः /
सङ्करी गुडपाके च(2) प्रतुदेत् परमर्मनुत् //
:न्
1 असिपत्रवने ऽग्निभिरिति ङ..
2 गुरुपाके चेति ख.. , ज.. च
:प् 244
203.m:
In Mahājvāla, one of evil intent [is punished]; on Krakaca, those who have intercourse with forbidden women; / a polluter of castes [is punished] in Guḍapāka; and one who pierces the vitals of others is pricked.
[Note]
1. 'asipatravane 'gnibhir iti' in manuscript ṅa.
2. 'gurupāke ceti' in manuscripts kha and ja.

203.s:
kṣārahrade(1) prāṇihantā kṣuradhāre ca bhūmihṛt /
ambarīṣe gosvarṇahṛd drumacchidvajraśastrake //
203.d:
क्षारह्रदे(1) प्राणिहन्ता क्षुरधारे च भूमिहृत् /
अम्बरीषे गोस्वर्णहृद् द्रुमच्छिद्वज्रशस्त्रके //
203.m: In Kṣārahrada, a killer of living creatures [is punished]; in Kṣuradhāra, a stealer of land; / in Ambarīṣa, a stealer of cows and gold; in Vajraśastraka, a feller of trees.

203.s:
madhuhartā parītāpe kālasūtre parārthahṛt /
kaśmale 'tyantamāṃsāśī ugragandhe hy apiṇḍadaḥ //
203.d:
मधुहर्ता परीतापे कालसूत्रे परार्थहृत् /
कश्मले ऽत्यन्तमांसाशी उग्रगन्धे ह्य् अपिण्डदः //
203.m: In Parītāpa, a stealer of honey; in Kālasūtra, a stealer of another's wealth; / in Kaśmala, one who excessively eats meat; and in Ugragandha, one who offers no ancestral food ball.

203.s:
durdhare tu kācabhakṣī vandigrāharatāś ca ye /
mañjuṣe narake lohe 'pratiṣṭhe śrutinindakaḥ //
203.d:
दुर्धरे तु काचभक्षी वन्दिग्राहरताश् च ये /
मञ्जुषे नरके लोहे ऽप्रतिष्ठे श्रुतिनिन्दकः //
203.m: In Durdhara, an eater of glass and those intent on capturing prisoners [are punished]; / in Mañjuṣa, the iron hell, and in Apratiṣṭha, a reviler of the Vedas.

203.s:
pūtivaktre kūṭasākṣī pariluṇṭhe dhanāpahā /
bālastrīvṛddhaghātī ca karāle brāhmaṇārtikṛt //
203.d:
पूतिवक्त्रे कूटसाक्षी परिलुण्ठे धनापहा /
बालस्त्रीवृद्धघाती च कराले ब्राह्मणार्तिकृत् //
203.m: In Pūtivaktra, a false witness; in Pariluṇṭha, a plunderer of wealth; / in Karāla, a killer of children, women, and the elderly, and one who torments a brahmin.

203.s: vilepe madyapo vipro mahātāmre tu medinaḥ(2) //20//
203.d: विलेपे मद्यपो विप्रो महाताम्रे तु मेदिनः(2) //20//
203.m: In Vilepa, a wine-drinking brahmin [is punished]; in Mahātāmra, the fat-eaters. //20

203.s:
tathākramya pāradārān jvalantīmāyasīṃ śilāṃ /
śālmalākhye tamāliṅgen nārī bahunaraṅgamā //
203.d:
तथाक्रम्य पारदारान् ज्वलन्तीमायसीं शिलां /
शाल्मलाख्ये तमालिङ्गेन् नारी बहुनरङ्गमा //
203.m: Likewise, an adulterer is forced to climb a blazing iron stone; / in the hell named Śālmala, a woman who consort with many men must embrace it.

203.s:
āsphoṭajihvoddharaṇaṃ strīkṣaṇān netrabhedanaṃ /
aṅgārarāśau kṣipyante mātṛputryādigāminaḥ //
203.d:
आस्फोटजिह्वोद्धरणं स्त्रीक्षणान् नेत्रभेदनं /
अङ्गारराशौ क्षिप्यन्ते मातृपुत्र्यादिगामिनः //
203.m: Tearing out the tongue by wrenching, and piercing the eyes for ogling women [are inflicted]; / those who have incestuous relations with a mother, daughter, and others are cast into a heap of burning coals.

203.s:
caurāḥ kṣuraiś ca bhidyante svamāṃsāśī ca māṃsabhuk /
māsopavāsakartā vai na yāti narakannaraḥ //
203.d:
चौराः क्षुरैश् च भिद्यन्ते स्वमांसाशी च मांसभुक् /
मासोपवासकर्ता वै न याति नरकन्नरः //
203.m: Thieves are slashed with razors, and a meat-eater is forced to eat his own flesh. / A person who observes a month-long fast does not go to hell,

203.s:
ekādaśīvratakaro bhīṣmapañcakasad vratī /
:e ity āgneye mahāpurāṇe narakasvarūpavarṇanaṃ nāma
tryadhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
:n
1 kṣārakūpe iti kha.. , cha.. ca
2 mahāprete tu bhedana iti kha.. , ga.. , gha.. , ḍa.. , cha.. , ja.. ca
:p 245
:ś atha caturadhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
māsopavāsavrataṃ
203.d:
एकादशीव्रतकरो भीष्मपञ्चकसद् व्रती /
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महापुराणे नरकस्वरूपवर्णनं नाम
त्र्यधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः ||
:न्
1 क्षारकूपे इति ख.. , छ.. च
2 महाप्रेते तु भेदन इति ख.. , ग.. , घ.. , ड.. , छ.. , ज.. च
:प् 245
:श् अथ चतुरधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः
मासोपवासव्रतं
203.m:
nor one who observes the Ekādaśī vow or keeps the noble vow of Bhīṣmapañcaka.
Thus in the Agni Mahāpurāṇa, the two hundred and third chapter, entitled 'The Description of the Nature of Hells'.
[Note]
1. 'kṣārakūpe iti' in manuscripts kha and cha.
2. 'mahāprete tu bhedana iti' in manuscripts kha, ga, gha, ḍa, cha, and ja.
Now, the two hundred and fourth chapter.
The votive observance of fasting for a month.

204.s:
agnir uvāca
vrataṃ māsopavāsañca(1) sarvotkṛṣṭaṃ vadāmi te /
kṛtvā tu vaiṣṇavaṃ yajñaṃ gurorājñāmavāpya ca //
204.d:
अग्निर् उवाच
व्रतं मासोपवासञ्च(1) सर्वोत्कृष्टं वदामि ते /
कृत्वा तु वैष्णवं यज्ञं गुरोराज्ञामवाप्य च //
204.m: Agni said: / I shall declare to you the votive observance of fasting for a month, which is the most supreme of all. / Having performed a Vaiṣṇava rite and having obtained the permission of one's guru,

204.s:
kṛcchrādyaiḥ svabalaṃ buddhvā kuryān māsopavāsakaṃ /
vānaprastho yatirvātha nārī vā vidhavā mune //
204.d:
कृच्छ्राद्यैः स्वबलं बुद्ध्वा कुर्यान् मासोपवासकं /
वानप्रस्थो यतिर्वाथ नारी वा विधवा मुने //
204.m: and having assessed one's own strength through rites like the kṛcchra penance, one should perform the month-long fast— / whether a forest hermit, an ascetic, or a widowed woman, O sage.

204.s:
āśvinasyāmale pakṣe ekādaśyāmupoṣitaḥ /
vratametattu gṛhṇīyādyāvattriṃśaddināni tu //
204.d:
आश्विनस्यामले पक्षे एकादश्यामुपोषितः /
व्रतमेतत्तु गृह्णीयाद्यावत्त्रिंशद्दिनानि तु //
204.m: Fasting on the eleventh lunar day of the bright fortnight of the month of Āśvina, / one should undertake this votive observance for thirty days,

204.s:
