गोवृषौ तु द्विजे दत्त्वा भुक्तिमुक्तिमवाप्नुयात् /
:न्
1 पापो इति ख.. , छ.. , ज.. च
2 सम्पूज्य वस्त्रगन्धाद्यैर् इति ङ..
:प् 267
रेवन्ताधिष्ठितञ्चाश्वं हैमं दत्त्वा न मृत्य्भाक् //
211.m:
Having given a cow and a bull to a twice-born, one attains worldly enjoyment and liberation.
[Notes]
[Note] 1: ‘pāpo’ thus in kha, cha, and ja.
[Variant readings].
And having given a golden horse mounted by Revanta, one does not suffer death.

211.s:
ghaṇṭādipūrṇamapyekaṃ dattvā syādbhuktimuktibhāk /
sarvān kāmānavāpnoti yaḥ prayacchati kāñcanaṃ //
211.d:
घण्टादिपूर्णमप्येकं दत्त्वा स्याद्भुक्तिमुक्तिभाक् /
सर्वान् कामानवाप्नोति यः प्रयच्छति काञ्चनं //
211.m: Even by giving a single [vessel] filled with bells and other [adornments], one partakes of worldly enjoyment and liberation. / Whoever gives gold attains all desires.

211.s:
suvarṇe dīyamāne tu rajataṃ dakṣiṇeṣyate /
anyeṣāmapi dānānāṃ suvarṇaṃ(1) dakṣiṇā smṛtā //
211.d:
सुवर्णे दीयमाने तु रजतं दक्षिणेष्यते /
अन्येषामपि दानानां सुवर्णं(1) दक्षिणा स्मृता //
211.m: When gold is being given, silver is prescribed as the sacrificial fee; / but for other gifts, gold is remembered as the sacrificial fee.

211.s:
suvarṇaṃ rajataṃ tāmraṃ taṇḍulaṃ dhānyameva ca /
nityaśrāddhaṃ devapūjā sarvametadadakṣiṇaṃ //
211.d:
सुवर्णं रजतं ताम्रं तण्डुलं धान्यमेव च /
नित्यश्राद्धं देवपूजा सर्वमेतददक्षिणं //
211.m: Gold, silver, copper, rice, grain, / the daily ancestral rite, and worship of the gods—all this is without a sacrificial fee.

211.s:
rajataṃ dakṣiṇā pitre dharmakāmārthasādhanaṃ /
suvarṇaṃ rajataṃ tāmraṃ maṇimuktāvasūni ca //
211.d:
रजतं दक्षिणा पित्रे धर्मकामार्थसाधनं /
सुवर्णं रजतं ताम्रं मणिमुक्तावसूनि च //
211.m: Silver is the sacrificial fee to the ancestors, achieving virtue, desire, and wealth. / Gold, silver, copper, jewels, pearls, and wealth—

211.s:
sarvametanmahāprājño dadāti vasudhāndadat /
pitṝṃś ca pitṛlokasthān devasthāne ca devatāḥ //
211.d:
सर्वमेतन्महाप्राज्ञो ददाति वसुधान्ददत् /
पितॄंश् च पितृलोकस्थान् देवस्थाने च देवताः //
211.m: all this the very wise man gives when giving land. / The ancestors residing in the realm of ancestors, and the deities in the abode of the gods—

211.s:
santarpayati śāntātmā yo dadāti vasundharām /
kharvaṭaṃ kheṭakaṃ vāpi grāmaṃ vā śasyaśālinaṃ //
211.d:
सन्तर्पयति शान्तात्मा यो ददाति वसुन्धराम् /
खर्वटं खेटकं वापि ग्रामं वा शस्यशालिनं //
211.m: the tranquil-minded man who gives land satisfies them [all]. / Whether an isolated market town, a hamlet, or a village rich in grain,

211.s:
nivartanaśataṃ vāpi tadardhaṃ vā gṛhādikaṃ /
api gocarmamātrāmbā dattvorvīṃ sarvabhāg bhavet //
211.d:
निवर्तनशतं वापि तदर्धं वा गृहादिकं /
अपि गोचर्ममात्राम्बा दत्त्वोर्वीं सर्वभाग् भवेत् //
211.m: or a hundred nivartanas, or half of that, or a house and the like, / or even giving land merely the size of a cow's hide, one partakes of everything.

211.s:
tailavinduryathā cāpsu prasarped bhūgataṃ tathā /
sarveṣāmevadānānamekajanmānugaṃ phalaṃ //
211.d:
तैलविन्दुर्यथा चाप्सु प्रसर्पेद् भूगतं तथा /
सर्वेषामेवदानानमेकजन्मानुगं फलं //
211.m: Just as a drop of oil spreads upon the water, so does [the merit] accrued from land. / The fruit of all other gifts follows [one] through a single birth;

211.s:
hāṭakakṣitigaurīṇāṃ saptajanmānugaṃ phalaṃ /
trisaptakulamuddhṛtya kanyādo brahmalokabhāk //
211.d:
हाटकक्षितिगौरीणां सप्तजन्मानुगं फलं /
त्रिसप्तकुलमुद्धृत्य कन्यादो ब्रह्मलोकभाक् //
211.m: the fruit of gold, land, and cows follows [one] through seven births. / Having delivered thrice seven families, the giver of a maiden partakes of the world of Brahmā.

211.s:
gajaṃ sadakṣiṇaṃ dattvā nirmalaḥ svargabhāg bhavet /
aśvaṃ dattvāyurārogyasaubhāgyasvargamāpnuyāt //
:n
1 hiraṇyamiti ṭa..
:p 268
211.d:
गजं सदक्षिणं दत्त्वा निर्मलः स्वर्गभाग् भवेत् /
अश्वं दत्त्वायुरारोग्यसौभाग्यस्वर्गमाप्नुयात् //
:न्
1 हिरण्यमिति ट..
:प् 268
211.m:
Having given an elephant along with a sacrificial fee, one becomes stainless and partakes of heaven. / Having given a horse, one obtains longevity, health, good fortune, and heaven.
[Note]
[Variant readings].

211.s:
dāsīṃ dattvā dvijendrāya apsarolokamāpnuyāt /
dattvā tāmramayīṃ sthālīṃ palānāṃ pañcabhiḥ śataiḥ //
211.d:
दासीं दत्त्वा द्विजेन्द्राय अप्सरोलोकमाप्नुयात् /
दत्त्वा ताम्रमयीं स्थालीं पलानां पञ्चभिः शतैः //
211.m: Having given a female servant to an eminent twice-born, one reaches the realm of the apsarases. / Having given a copper cooking vessel made of five hundred palas,

211.s:
ardhaistadardhair ardhair vā bhuktimuktimavāpnuyāt(1) /
śakaṭaṃ vṛṣasaṃyuktaṃ dattvā yānena nākabhāk //
211.d:
अर्धैस्तदर्धैर् अर्धैर् वा भुक्तिमुक्तिमवाप्नुयात्(1) /
शकटं वृषसंयुक्तं दत्त्वा यानेन नाकभाक् //
211.m: or half of that, or half of that, or half of that, one attains worldly enjoyment and liberation. / Having given a cart yoked with bulls, one partakes of heaven with a chariot.

211.s:
vastradānāllabhedāyurārogyaṃ svargamakṣayaṃ /
dhānyagodhūmakalamayavādīn svargabhāg dadat //
211.d:
वस्त्रदानाल्लभेदायुरारोग्यं स्वर्गमक्षयं /
धान्यगोधूमकलमयवादीन् स्वर्गभाग् ददत् //
211.m: From the gift of clothing, one gains longevity, health, and imperishable heaven. / Giving grain, wheat, rice, barley, and the like, one partakes of heaven.

211.s:
āsanaṃ taijasaṃ pātraṃ lavaṇaṃ gandhacandanaṃ /
dhūpaṃ dīpañca tāmvūlaṃ lohaṃ rūpyañca ratnakaṃ(2) //
211.d:
आसनं तैजसं पात्रं लवणं गन्धचन्दनं /
धूपं दीपञ्च ताम्वूलं लोहं रूप्यञ्च रत्नकं(2) //
211.m: A seat, a metallic vessel, salt, fragrant unguents and sandalwood, / incense, a lamp, betel, iron, silver, and a jewel—

211.s:
divyāni nānādravyāṇi dattvā syād bhuktimuktibhāk /
tilāṃś ca tilapātrañca dattvā svargamavāpnuyāt //
211.d:
दिव्यानि नानाद्रव्याणि दत्त्वा स्याद् भुक्तिमुक्तिभाक् /
तिलांश् च तिलपात्रञ्च दत्त्वा स्वर्गमवाप्नुयात् //
211.m: giving various divine substances, one partakes of worldly enjoyment and liberation. / Having given sesame seeds and a vessel of sesame, one attains heaven.

211.s:
annadānāt paraṃ nāsti na bhūtaṃ na bhaviṣyati /
hastyaśvarathadānāni dāsīdāsagṛhāṇi ca //
211.d:
अन्नदानात् परं नास्ति न भूतं न भविष्यति /
हस्त्यश्वरथदानानि दासीदासगृहाणि च //
211.m: There is no gift higher than the gift of food, nor has there been, nor will there be. / Gifts of elephants, horses, and chariots, and female and male servants and houses—

211.s:
annadānasya sarvāṇi kalāṃ nārhanti ṣoḍaśīṃ /
kṛtvāpi sumahatpāpaṃ yaḥ paścādannado bhavet //
211.d:
अन्नदानस्य सर्वाणि कलां नार्हन्ति षोडशीं /
कृत्वापि सुमहत्पापं यः पश्चादन्नदो भवेत् //
211.m: all of them do not equal a sixteenth part of the gift of food. / Even having committed a very great sin, one who afterwards becomes a giver of food

211.s:
sarvapāpavinirmukto lokānāpnoti cākṣayān /
pānīyañca prapāndattvā bhuktimuktimavāpnuyāt //
211.d:
सर्वपापविनिर्मुक्तो लोकानाप्नोति चाक्षयान् /
पानीयञ्च प्रपान्दत्त्वा भुक्तिमुक्तिमवाप्नुयात् //
211.m: is freed from all sins and attains imperishable worlds. / Giving drinking water and a water-dispensing booth, one attains worldly enjoyment and liberation.

211.s:
agniṃ kāṣṭhañca mārgādau dattvā dīptyādimāpnuyāt(3) /
devagandharvanārībhirvimāne sevyate divi //
211.d:
अग्निं काष्ठञ्च मार्गादौ दत्त्वा दीप्त्यादिमाप्नुयात्(3) /
देवगन्धर्वनारीभिर्विमाने सेव्यते दिवि //
211.m: Giving fire and firewood on roads and similar places, one obtains radiance and the like; / he is attended upon in heaven by the women of gods and gandharvas on a celestial vehicle.

211.s:
ghṛtaṃ taikañca lavaṇaṃ dattvā sarvamavāpnuyāt /
:n
1 tatordhvatastadardhārdhair yuktāṃ bhuktimavāpnuyāt iti cha..
2 dhūpadīpañca naivedyaṃ tāmvūlaṃ loharatnakamiti kha..
3 dīptāgnimāpnuyāditi ṅa..
:p 269
chatropānahakāṣṭhādi dattvā svarge sukhī vaset(1) //
211.d:
घृतं तैकञ्च लवणं दत्त्वा सर्वमवाप्नुयात् /
:न्
1 ततोर्ध्वतस्तदर्धार्धैर् युक्तां भुक्तिमवाप्नुयात् इति छ..
2 धूपदीपञ्च नैवेद्यं ताम्वूलं लोहरत्नकमिति ख..
3 दीप्ताग्निमाप्नुयादिति ङ..
:प् 269
छत्रोपानहकाष्ठादि दत्त्वा स्वर्गे सुखी वसेत्(1) //
211.m:
Giving clarified butter, oil, and salt, one obtains everything.
[Note]
[Variant readings].
[Variant readings].
[Variant readings].
Giving an umbrella, shoes, firewood, and the like, one dwells happily in heaven.

211.s:
pratipattithimukhyeṣu viṣkumbhādikayogake /
caitrādau vatsarādau ca aśvinyādau hariṃ haraṃ //
211.d:
प्रतिपत्तिथिमुख्येषु विष्कुम्भादिकयोगके /
चैत्रादौ वत्सरादौ च अश्विन्यादौ हरिं हरं //
211.m: On prominent lunar days such as the first lunar day, during astrological yogas beginning with Viṣkumbha, / at the beginning of Caitra and the beginning of the year, under Aśvinī and the rest, having worshipped Hari, Hara,

211.s:
brahmāṇaṃ lokapālādīn prārcya dānaṃ mahāphalaṃ /
vṛkṣārāmān bhojanādīn mārgasaṃvāhanādikān //
211.d:
ब्रह्माणं लोकपालादीन् प्रार्च्य दानं महाफलं /
वृक्षारामान् भोजनादीन् मार्गसंवाहनादिकान् //
211.m: Brahmā, the world guardians, and others, a gift yields great fruit. / Trees, groves, meals and the like, massaging on the road and the like,

211.s:
pādābhyaṅgādikaṃ dattvā bhuktimuktimavāpnuyāt /
trīṇi tulyaphalānīha gāvaḥ pṛthvī sarasvatī //
211.d:
पादाभ्यङ्गादिकं दत्त्वा भुक्तिमुक्तिमवाप्नुयात् /
त्रीणि तुल्यफलानीह गावः पृथ्वी सरस्वती //
211.m: and giving foot anointment and the like, one attains worldly enjoyment and liberation. / Three things yield equal fruit here: cows, the earth, and Sarasvatī.

211.s:
vrāhmīṃ sarasvatīndattvā nirmalo brahmalokabhāk /
saptadvīpamahīdaḥ sa brahmajñānaṃ dadāti yaḥ //
211.d:
व्राह्मीं सरस्वतीन्दत्त्वा निर्मलो ब्रह्मलोकभाक् /
सप्तद्वीपमहीदः स ब्रह्मज्ञानं ददाति यः //
211.m: Having given sacred Vedic learning, one becomes spotless and partakes of the world of Brahmā. / He who gives knowledge of Brahman is a giver of the earth with its seven continents.

211.s:
abhayaṃ sarvabhūtebhyo yo dadyāt sarvabhāṅ naraḥ /
purāṇaṃ bhārataṃ vāpi rāmāyaṇamathāpi vā //
211.d:
अभयं सर्वभूतेभ्यो यो दद्यात् सर्वभाङ् नरः /
पुराणं भारतं वापि रामायणमथापि वा //
211.m: A man who grants freedom from fear to all beings partakes of all things. / Having written down a Purāṇa, or the Mahābhārata, or the Rāmāyaṇa,

211.s:
likhitvā pustakaṃ dattvā bhuktimuktimavāpnuyāt /
vedaśāstraṃ nṛtyagītaṃ yo 'dhyāpayati nākabhāk //
211.d:
लिखित्वा पुस्तकं दत्त्वा भुक्तिमुक्तिमवाप्नुयात् /
वेदशास्त्रं नृत्यगीतं यो ऽध्यापयति नाकभाक् //
211.m: and given the book, one attains worldly enjoyment and liberation. / One who teaches the Veda and śāstras, dance and song, partakes of heaven.

211.s:
vittaṃ dadyādupādhyāye chātrāṇāṃ bhojanādikaṃ /
kimadattaṃ bhavettena dharmakāmādidarśinā //
211.d:
वित्तं दद्यादुपाध्याये छात्राणां भोजनादिकं /
किमदत्तं भवेत्तेन धर्मकामादिदर्शिना //
211.m: One should give wealth to the teacher, and food and the like to the students; / what would be ungiven by him who perceives virtue, desire, and the rest?

211.s:
vājapeyasahasrasya samyagdattasya yat phalaṃ /
tatphalaṃ sarvamāpnoti vidyādānanna saṃśayaḥ //
211.d:
वाजपेयसहस्रस्य सम्यग्दत्तस्य यत् फलं /
तत्फलं सर्वमाप्नोति विद्यादानन्न संशयः //
211.m: Whatever fruit comes from a thousand properly offered Vājapeya sacrifices, / all that fruit one obtains from the gift of knowledge, without doubt.

211.s:
śivālaye viṣṇugṛhe sūryasya bhavane tathā /
sarvadānapradaḥ sa syāt pustakaṃ vācayettu yaḥ //
211.d:
शिवालये विष्णुगृहे सूर्यस्य भवने तथा /
सर्वदानप्रदः स स्यात् पुस्तकं वाचयेत्तु यः //
211.m: In a temple of Śiva, in a house of Viṣṇu, and likewise in a shrine of Sūrya, / he who has a book recited becomes a giver of all gifts.

211.s:
trailokye caturo varṇāś catvāraścāśramāḥ pṛthak /
brahmādyā devatāḥ sarvā vidyādāne pratiṣṭhatāḥ //
:n
1 svarge mahīyate iti ga.. / svarge sukhī bhavedeti gha.. , ṅa.. ca
:p 270
211.d:
त्रैलोक्ये चतुरो वर्णाश् चत्वारश्चाश्रमाः पृथक् /
ब्रह्माद्या देवताः सर्वा विद्यादाने प्रतिष्ठताः //
:न्
1 स्वर्गे महीयते इति ग.. / स्वर्गे सुखी भवेदेति घ.. , ङ.. च
:प् 270
211.m:
The four social classes and four stages of life separately in the three worlds, / and all the deities headed by Brahmā, are established in the gift of knowledge.
[Note]
[Variant readings].

211.s:
vidyā kāmadughā dhenurvidyā cakṣuranuttamaṃ /
upavedapradānena gandharvaiḥ saha modate //
211.d:
विद्या कामदुघा धेनुर्विद्या चक्षुरनुत्तमं /
उपवेदप्रदानेन गन्धर्वैः सह मोदते //
211.m: Knowledge is a wish-fulfilling cow; knowledge is the unsurpassed eye. / Through the gift of an Upaveda, one rejoices with the gandharvas.

211.s:
vedāṅgānāñca dānena svargalokamavāpnuyāt /
dharmaśāstrapradānena dharmeṇa saha modate //
211.d:
वेदाङ्गानाञ्च दानेन स्वर्गलोकमवाप्नुयात् /
धर्मशास्त्रप्रदानेन धर्मेण सह मोदते //
211.m: Through the gift of the limbs of the Veda, one attains the heavenly world. / Through the gift of a treatise on dharma, one rejoices with Dharma.

211.s:
siddhāntānāṃ pradānena mokṣamāpnotyasaṃśayaṃ /
vidyādānamavāpnoti pradānāt pustakasya tu //
211.d:
सिद्धान्तानां प्रदानेन मोक्षमाप्नोत्यसंशयं /
विद्यादानमवाप्नोति प्रदानात् पुस्तकस्य तु //
211.m: Through the gift of philosophical treatises, one undoubtedly attains liberation. / But one obtains [the merit of] the gift of knowledge through the donation of a manuscript.

211.s:
śāstrāṇi ca purāṇāni dattvā sarvamavāpnuyāt /
śiṣyāṃś ca śikṣayedyastu puṇḍalīkaphalaṃ labhet //
211.d:
शास्त्राणि च पुराणानि दत्त्वा सर्वमवाप्नुयात् /
शिष्यांश् च शिक्षयेद्यस्तु पुण्डलीकफलं लभेत् //
211.m: Having given treatises and Purāṇas, one attains everything. / But one who instructs students obtains the fruit of a puṇḍarīka sacrifice.

211.s:
yena jīvati taddattvā phalasyānto na vidyate /
loke sreṣṭhatamaṃ sarvamātmanaścāpi yat priyaṃ //
211.d:
येन जीवति तद्दत्त्वा फलस्यान्तो न विद्यते /
लोके स्रेष्ठतमं सर्वमात्मनश्चापि यत् प्रियं //
211.m: Giving that by which one lives, there is no end to the fruit. / Whatever is best in the world and whatever is dear to oneself,

211.s:
sarvaṃ pitṝṇāṃ dātavyaṃ teṣāmevākṣayārthinā /
viṣṇuṃ rudraṃ padmayoniṃ devīvighneśvarādikān //
211.d:
सर्वं पितॄणां दातव्यं तेषामेवाक्षयार्थिना /
विष्णुं रुद्रं पद्मयोनिं देवीविघ्नेश्वरादिकान् //
211.m: all that should be given to the ancestors by one desiring imperishable merit for them. / Having worshipped Viṣṇu, Rudra, the lotus-born [Brahmā], the Goddess, the Lord of Obstacles, and others,

211.s:
pūjayitvā pradadyādyaḥ pūjādravyaṃ sa sarvabhāk /
devālayaṃ ca pratimāṃ kārayat sarvamāpnuyāt //
211.d:
पूजयित्वा प्रदद्याद्यः पूजाद्रव्यं स सर्वभाक् /
देवालयं च प्रतिमां कारयत् सर्वमाप्नुयात् //
211.m: he who offers the articles of worship partakes of everything. / Causing a temple and an image to be made, one obtains everything.

211.s:
sammārjanaṃ copalepaṃ kurvan syānnirmalaḥ pumān /
nānāmaṇḍalakāryagre maṇḍalādhipatirbhavet(1) //
211.d:
सम्मार्जनं चोपलेपं कुर्वन् स्यान्निर्मलः पुमान् /
नानामण्डलकार्यग्रे मण्डलाधिपतिर्भवेत्(1) //
211.m: Performing sweeping and plastering [the ground], a man becomes spotless. / Making various maṇḍalas in front [of the deity], he becomes the ruler of a province.

211.s:
gandhaṃ puṣpaṃ dhūpadīpaṃ naivedyañca pradakṣiṇaṃ /
ghaṇṭādhvajavitānañca prekṣaṇaṃ vādyagautakaṃ //
211.d:
गन्धं पुष्पं धूपदीपं नैवेद्यञ्च प्रदक्षिणं /
घण्टाध्वजवितानञ्च प्रेक्षणं वाद्यगौतकं //
211.m: Fragrance, flowers, incense, a lamp, food offerings, circumambulation, / a bell, a banner, a canopy, a dramatic spectacle, instrumental music, and song,

211.s:
vastrādidattvādevāya bhuktimuktimavāpnuyāt /
kastūrikāṃ śihlakañca śrīkhaṇḍamagurūntathā //
211.d:
वस्त्रादिदत्त्वादेवाय भुक्तिमुक्तिमवाप्नुयात् /
कस्तूरिकां शिह्लकञ्च श्रीखण्डमगुरून्तथा //
211.m: and having given garments and other things to the deity, one attains worldly enjoyment and liberation. / Musk, olibanum, sandalwood, and aloe-wood as well,

211.s:
karpūrañca tathāmustaṃ gugguluṃ vijayaṃ dadet /
:n
1 sammārjanamityādiḥ maṇḍalādhipatirbhavedityantaḥ pāṭhaḥ
ja.. pustake nāsti
:p 271
ghṛtaprasthena saṃsthāpya saṅkrāntyādau sa sarvabhāk //
211.d:
कर्पूरञ्च तथामुस्तं गुग्गुलुं विजयं ददेत् /
:न्
1 सम्मार्जनमित्यादिः मण्डलाधिपतिर्भवेदित्यन्तः पाठः
ज.. पुस्तके नास्ति
:प् 271
घृतप्रस्थेन संस्थाप्य सङ्क्रान्त्यादौ स सर्वभाक् //
211.m:
camphor, mustā grass, guggulu, and cannabis one should give.
[Note]
[Variant readings].
Installing [the deity] with a prastha of clarified butter on a solstice or equinox and the like, he partakes of everything.

211.s:
snānaṃ palaśataṃ jñeyamabhyaṅgaṃ pañcaviṃśatiḥ /
palānāntu sahasreṇa mahāsnānaṃ prakīrtitaṃ //
211.d:
स्नानं पलशतं ज्ञेयमभ्यङ्गं पञ्चविंशतिः /
पलानान्तु सहस्रेण महास्नानं प्रकीर्तितं //
211.m: A bath should be known as one hundred palas, and an anointing as twenty-five; / but with a thousand palas, a great bath is proclaimed.

211.s:
daśāparādhāstoyena kṣīreṇa snāpanācchataṃ /
sahasraṃ payasā dadhnā ghṛtenāyutamiṣyate //
211.d:
दशापराधास्तोयेन क्षीरेण स्नापनाच्छतं /
सहस्रं पयसा दध्ना घृतेनायुतमिष्यते //
211.m: Ten offences [are removed] by bathing with water, a hundred by bathing with milk; / a thousand are considered [removed] by milk-curd, and ten thousand by clarified butter.

211.s:
dāsīdāsamalaṅkāraṃ gobhūmyaśvagajādikaṃ /
devāya dattvā saubhāgyaṃ dhanāyuṣmān vrajeddivaṃ //
:e ity āgneye mahāpurāṇe nānādānāni
nāmaikādaśādhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
:ś atha dvādaśādhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
merudānāni
211.d:
दासीदासमलङ्कारं गोभूम्यश्वगजादिकं /
देवाय दत्त्वा सौभाग्यं धनायुष्मान् व्रजेद्दिवं //
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महापुराणे नानादानानि
नामैकादशाधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः ||
:श् अथ द्वादशाधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः
मेरुदानानि
211.m:
Having given female and male slaves, ornaments, cows, land, horses, elephants, and the like / to the god, a person endowed with fortune, wealth, and long life goes to heaven.
Thus ends the two hundred and eleventh chapter, entitled "Various Gifts", in the great Agni Purāṇa.
Now begins the two hundred and twelfth chapter.
Gifts of Mount Meru
